links.title: Protect Turkish Street Dogs
links.mailtoSubject: Yasadışı sokak köpekleri ve kedilerinin öldürülmesini durdurun/Stop illegal street-dog and cat killings
links.description:
On July 30th, 2024, Turkish lawmakers passed a law that mandated that stray dogs be removed from the streets.
Thousands of dogs are being poisoned and thrown into mass graves, run over by cars, beaten to death in the streets, and dumped on the edge of the mountain without food or shelter.
The ones that end up in overcrowded shelters will either be euthanized or starve to death due to a complete disregard for their care.

TNVR programs work in reducing stray populations and in eliminating the spread of rabies, but it's cheaper to kill them. Proving that money is more important than life in Turkey.

Turkey's tourism industry is projected to earn $64 billion in 2025.
Boycott Turkey and hit them where it hurts them the most, their wallet. Stop purchasing Turkish goods, and cancel your vacations for somewhere more humane, like Spain or Portugal. 

#Turkey #dogsofinstagram #doglovers

İlgili makamlara,

Bu mektup, Türkiye genelinde sokak köpek ve kedilerinin yasadışı olarak yakalanması, istismar edilmesi ve öldürülmesine ilişkin yaygın ve belgelenmiş raporlarla ilgili resmi bir şikayet mektubudur.

Bu, kamera önünde açıkça gerçekleştirilen bir zulümdür ve şu anda ulusal bir hesap verebilirlik ve itibar krizine dönüşmüştür.

Raporlar ve görüntüler tekrar tekrar şunları göstermektedir:

* kamuya açık alanlarda zehirlenme ve toplu ölümler
* toplama sırasında köpek ve kedilerin dövülmesi, vurulması veya şiddet uygulanması
* yasal veterinerlik gerekçesi olmaksızın hayvanların öldürülmesi
* şeffaf kayıtlar tutulmaksızın cesetlerin kaldırılması ve imha edilmesi
* bağımsız erişim veya kamu denetimi olmaksızın faaliyet gösteren barınaklar

Türkiye'nin hayvan koruma çerçevesi, “kamu güvenliği” bahanesiyle yasadışı öldürme, zulüm veya hesap verilmeyen imhaya izin vermemektedir. Ötenazi uygulanacaksa, bu yasal, kanıta dayalı ve veterinerlik otoritesi altında yapılmalı, belediyeler veya yükleniciler için bir kestirme yol olmamalıdır.

TALEPLERİMİZ (ACİL, GÖRÜNÜR EYLEM)

1. Tüm belediyeler ve yükleniciler aşağıdakileri derhal durdurmalıdır:

* zehirleme (yemleme dahil)
* toplama sırasında hayvanları vurma, dövme veya yaralama
* belgelenmiş veteriner kararı olmadan öldürme
* kayıtsız ölümler ve imha

2. Ulusal makamlar, suçlanan belediyeler ve yükleniciler hakkında soruşturma açmalı ve kanıtların desteklediği durumlarda cezai ve idari yaptırımlar uygulamalıdır.
   “Dahili olarak ele alınmak” hesap verebilirlik değildir. Bu, örtbas etmektir.

3. Kamuya ait hayvanları barındıran tesisler aşağıdakilere izin vermelidir:

* bağımsız denetim
* doğrulanmış STK erişimi
* hayvan başına denetlenebilir gözetim zinciri

KAMU GÜVENLİĞİ GERÇEĞİ: BİR TÜRÜ İSTİKRARSIZLAŞTIRMAK GÜVENLİK SAĞLAMAZ

Sokak hayvanlarının popülasyonları agresif bir şekilde ortadan kaldırıldıkça, sıçanlar, yılanlar, yaban domuzları ve kurtların kentsel alanlara daha yakın yerlerde görülmeye başladığı yaygın olarak gözlemlenmiştir. Tek bir neden öne sürülmese bile, ilke basittir: Bir ortamdan uzun süredir var olan türleri ortadan kaldırdığınızda, gelişmiş bir ekosistemi bozarsınız ve istenmeyen sonuçlar yaratırsınız.

* Sıçanlar hastalık taşır ve yiyecek atıkları bulunan ve avcıların baskısının azaldığı yerlerde çoğalır.
* Yılanlar avlarının bulunduğu yerleri takip ederler ve Türkiye'de zehirli yerli türler vardır.
* Yaban domuzları ve kurtlar “canavar” değildir, ancak kışkırtıldıklarında, tehdit edildiklerinde veya köşeye sıkıştırıldıklarında kendilerini savunabilirler ve savunurlar.

Köpekleri ve kedileri ortadan kaldırmak riski ortadan kaldırmaz, halkın maruz kaldığı şeyi değiştirir. Diğer hayvanların dolduracağı bir boşluk bırakır ve istikrarsızlık ve yetersiz atık kontrolü nedeniyle tehlikeyi artırır.

ÇÖZÜM TNVR'DIR, ZULÜM DEĞİL

Sıkı ve doğru bir şekilde uygulanan TNVR programı (yakalama, kısırlaştırma, aşılama ve geri bırakma), zamanla üremeyi azaltan, aşılama kapsamı sayesinde kuduz riskini azaltan ve hayvan sayısının doğal olarak azalmasıyla ekosistemin kademeli olarak uyum sağlamasına olanak tanıyan tek yaklaşımdır.

Şiddet içeren toplu uzaklaştırma ve “temizlik” operasyonları, kargaşa, panik, yerinden edilme ve tekrarlanan acı döngüleri yaratır. Bu da halkı daha güvende değil, daha güvensiz hale getirir.

ŞU AN BEKLEDİKLERİMİZ

* Köpek ve kedilerin yasadışı olarak öldürülmesinin derhal durdurulduğunu teyit eden bir kamuoyu açıklaması
* Yayınlanmış bir ulusal uygulama planı ve denetim çerçevesi
* Yayınlanmış belediye sonuç raporları (sayılar, yükleniciler, gözaltında ölümler)
* Videoda zulüm yaparken yakalanan herkes için gerçek sonuçlar

Yanıt vermeme, reddetme olarak değerlendirilecektir. Sessizlik, onay olarak değerlendirilecektir.

Saygılarımızla,

@HallieForAnimals Ekibi
contact@hallieforanimals.org

To whom it may concern,

This is a formal escalation regarding widespread, documented reports of street dogs and cats being unlawfully captured, abused, and killed across Türkiye.

This is cruelty on camera, carried out openly, and it is now a national accountability and reputational crisis.

Reports and footage repeatedly show:

* poisoning and mass die-offs in public areas
* dogs and cats beaten, shot, or violently handled during collection
* animals killed without lawful veterinary justification
* bodies removed and disposed of without transparent records
* shelters operating without independent access or public oversight

Türkiye’s animal protection framework does not permit illegal killing, cruelty, or unaccountable disposal under the cover of “public safety.” If euthanasia occurs, it must be lawful, evidence-based, and under veterinary authority not a shortcut for municipalities or contractors.

WHAT WE ARE DEMANDING (IMMEDIATE, VISIBLE ACTION)

1. All municipalities and contractors must immediately cease:

* poisoning (including baiting)
* shooting, beating, or injuring animals during collection
* killing without documented veterinary decision-making
* unrecorded deaths and disposal

2. National authorities must open investigations into implicated municipalities and contractors and pursue criminal and administrative penalties where evidence supports it.
   “Handled internally” is not accountability. It is concealment.

3. Facilities holding public animals must allow:

* independent inspection
* verified NGO access
* auditable chain-of-custody per animal

PUBLIC SAFETY REALITY: DESTABILISING ONE SPECIES DOES NOT CREATE SAFETY

It has been widely noted that rats, snakes, boar, and wolves are appearing closer to urban areas as street animal populations are aggressively removed. Even without claiming a single cause, the principle is simple: when you remove long-established species from an environment, you disrupt a developed ecosystem and create unintended consequences.

* Rats carry disease and thrive where food waste is available and pressure from predators decreases.
* Snakes follow prey availability, and Türkiye has venomous native species.
* Wild boar and wolves are not “monsters,” but they can and will defend themselves if provoked, threatened, or cornered.

Removing dogs and cats does not eliminate risk — it changes what the public is exposed to. It leaves a vacuum that other animals will fill, and it increases danger through instability and poor waste control.

THE SOLUTION IS TNVR NOT CRUELTY

A strict, properly enforced TNVR program (trap neuter vaccinate return) is the only approach that reduces breeding over time, reduces rabies risk through vaccination coverage, and allows the ecosystem to adapt gradually as animal numbers naturally decline.

Violent mass removals and “clean-ups” create churn, panic, displacement, and repeated cycles of suffering. while leaving the public less safe, not more safe.

WHAT WE EXPECT NOW

* A public statement confirming an immediate halt to illegal killings of dogs and cats
* A published national enforcement plan and inspection framework
* Published municipal outcome reporting (numbers, contractors, deaths in custody)
* Real consequences for anyone caught on video committing cruelty

Non-response will be treated as refusal. Silence will be treated as consent.

Sincerely,

@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
A quien corresponda:

Les escribimos para llamar urgentemente la atención sobre un incidente profundamente preocupante ocurrido en Arica, Chile, donde un perro indefenso llamado Blanquito fue atropellado por un vehículo de los Carabineros y abandonado sin recibir asistencia. Este acto de negligencia, captado por las cámaras de seguridad, muestra cómo el vehículo no se detuvo a pesar de las súplicas desesperadas de los transeúntes. Blanquito, que no representaba ninguna amenaza y simplemente se encontraba fuera de su casa, sufre ahora lesiones graves y está hospitalizado, luchando por su vida.

Este incidente no solo constituye una violación de la compasión básica, sino también un claro incumplimiento de la responsabilidad encomendada a las fuerzas del orden de proteger y servir a todos los miembros de la comunidad, incluidos los más vulnerables. La falta de asistencia y el desprecio por la indignación pública exigen una rendición de cuentas inmediata.

Le instamos a:

1. Iniciar una investigación exhaustiva y transparente sobre este incidente, garantizando que los responsables rindan cuentas.
2. Implementar protocolos más estrictos para la conducción de vehículos y la respuesta a incidentes relacionados con el bienestar animal en los que se vean implicados vehículos institucionales.
3. Abordar públicamente este caso, asegurando a la comunidad que no se tolerará tal negligencia y que se están tomando medidas para evitar que se repita en el futuro.

La historia de Blanquito ha tenido un gran impacto entre los defensores de los animales y los ciudadanos preocupados de todo el mundo. Nos mantenemos unidos para exigir justicia y un cambio sistémico que proteja a los animales de cualquier daño y garantice que quienes ocupan puestos de autoridad mantengan los más altos estándares de integridad y compasión.

Solicitamos una declaración pública inmediata en la que se describan las medidas que su oficina u organización tomará para abordar este asunto. El mundo está pendiente de ello, y no descansaremos hasta que se haga justicia.

Prueba en vídeo: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1L9UjinErACrcapyje5vAb_bLWAb5hCE4/view?usp=sharing

Atentamente,



El equipo de @HallieForAnimals
contact@hallieforanimals.org




To Whom It May Concern,

We are writing to bring urgent attention to a deeply troubling incident that occurred in Arica, Chile, where a defenseless dog named Blanquito was struck by a Carabineros vehicle and left abandoned without aid. This act of negligence, captured on CCTV, shows the vehicle failing to stop despite the desperate pleas of bystanders. Blanquito, who posed no threat and was simply outside his home, now suffers from severe injuries and is hospitalized, fighting for his life.

This incident is not only a violation of basic compassion but also a clear breach of the responsibility entrusted to law enforcement to protect and serve all members of the community—including our most vulnerable. The failure to render aid and the disregard for public outcry demand immediate accountability.

We urge you to:

1. Launch a thorough and transparent investigation into this incident, ensuring those responsible are held accountable.
2. Implement stricter protocols for vehicle operation and response to animal welfare incidents involving institutional vehicles.
3. Publicly address this case, reassuring the community that such negligence will not be tolerated and that steps are being taken to prevent future occurrences.

Blanquito’s story has resonated deeply with animal advocates and concerned citizens worldwide. We stand united in demanding justice and systemic change to protect animals from harm and ensure that those in positions of authority uphold the highest standards of integrity and compassion.

We request a prompt public statements outlining the actions your office or organization will take to address this matter. The world is watching, and we will not rest until justice is served.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1L9UjinErACrcapyje5vAb_bLWAb5hCE4/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

The recent federal indictment of Kristine Michelle Hicks for unlicensed animal dealing, wire fraud, and animal cruelty presents a critical opportunity for Texas to send an unequivocal message: 
Animal abuse will not be tolerated, and those who commit such acts will face the full force of the law.

- Animal abuse is a proven predictor of violent crime. Research shows that 70% of animal abusers have committed other criminal offenses, and nearly 40% have committed violent crimes against people.
- The FBI tracks animal cruelty alongside felony crimes like arson, assault, and homicide, recognizing its role as a “predictor crime” for future violence.
- In households where animal abuse occurs, there is an 88% overlap with child abuse and a 70%+ overlap with domestic violence.
- Hicks’ actions—shooting a dog tied to a tree, operating an unlicensed breeding facility, and defrauding buyers—demonstrate a pattern of cruelty and deception that cannot go unpunished.

We Demand:

1. Maximum penalties for Kristine Michelle Hicks under federal and state law, reflecting the severity of her crimes and serving as a deterrent to others.
2. Public accountability to ensure transparency in the legal process and restore faith in our justice system.
3. Strengthened enforcement of animal welfare laws to prevent future abuses and protect vulnerable animals and families.

We urge you to take immediate action to ensure Hicks is held fully accountable. The eyes of Texas, the nation, and the world are watching.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1TE4gpazpqyzQj1uEie__eeMR_X3EQ8lw/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

P.S. For further reading on the link between animal abuse and violent crime, see the FBI’s Law Enforcement Bulletin: The Link Between Animal Cruelty and Human Violence: https://leb.fbi.gov/articles/featured-articles/the-link-between-animal-cruelty-and-human-violence

links.title: Stop The Cat & Dog Meat Trade in Vietnam
links.mailtoSubject: Việt Nam phải chấm dứt hoạt động buôn bán thịt chó và mèo tàn bạo/Vietnam Must End the Brutal Dog and Cat Meat Trade
links.description:
PLEASE SEND THE ONE-CLICK EMAIL IN MY LINKTREE TO VIETNAMESE AUTHORITIES TITLED "STOP THE CAT & DOG MEAT TRADE IN VIETNAM"❗️

In Vietnam, an estimated 6 million dogs and 1 million cats are slaughtered for meat every year. Animals are stolen from the streets and from the homes of families, pets ripped from their owners' gardens, still wearing their collars. They're transported for hours or days in wire cages, without food or water, piled on top of one another. They're killed by electrocution, by bludgeoning, and by throat-cutting, often while fully conscious.
The dog and cat meat trade isn't a controlled industry; it operates in the open, in markets and restaurants, largely unchallenged by law. Despite growing opposition from younger Vietnamese generations and repeated calls from international animal welfare organisations, the Vietnamese government has failed to act. Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City have issued non-binding requests to end the trade, but without legislation, they're meaningless.
The trade is a significant driver of rabies and cholera outbreaks, posing a direct public health risk to both Vietnamese citizens and the millions of tourists who visit each year. TNVR programs have proven effective in managing stray populations and controlling the spread of disease, but it's more profitable to steal, cage, and kill.
Vietnam's tourism industry generated over $23 billion in 2024 and is growing fast. Boycott Vietnam until its government acts. Stop purchasing Vietnamese goods, and redirect your travel money to countries that don't profit from the suffering of companion animals.

#animallover #Vietnam #doglover

links.mailtoBody:
Kính gửi quý vị,

Chúng tôi viết thư này với tư cách là những công dân toàn cầu, những người bảo vệ động vật và những cá nhân quan tâm, để yêu cầu cấm hoàn toàn và ngay lập tức hoạt động buôn bán thịt chó và mèo tại Việt Nam. Ngành công nghiệp tàn nhẫn và lạc hậu này không chỉ gây ra những đau khổ không thể tưởng tượng được cho hàng triệu con vật, mà còn đe dọa sức khỏe cộng đồng, làm tổn hại đến uy tín quốc tế của Việt Nam, và đi ngược lại các giá trị của một xã hội hiện đại, giàu lòng nhân ái.

- Hơn sáu triệu con chó và một triệu con mèo bị giết mổ dã man tại Việt Nam mỗi năm. Hầu hết những con vật này là thú cưng bị đánh cắp hoặc động vật trong cộng đồng, bị tách khỏi nhà và gia đình, chỉ để phải đối mặt với những điều kiện khủng khiếp, bị nhốt chật chội trong lồng, bị bỏ đói và phải chịu những phương pháp giết mổ tàn bạo.
- Công dân Việt Nam áp đảo phản đối ngành công nghiệp này. Một cuộc khảo sát năm 2021 của FOUR PAWS cho thấy 91% người Việt Nam cho rằng ngành công nghiệp này nên bị cấm hoặc hạn chế, và 95% khẳng định nó không phải là một phần của văn hóa Việt Nam. Các thành phố như Hà Nội đã bắt đầu thực hiện các bước để loại bỏ việc tiêu thụ thịt chó, chứng minh rằng sự thay đổi là có thể và được mong đợi.
- Hoạt động buôn bán này chủ yếu diễn ra ngoài vòng pháp luật. Mặc dù có các quy định hiện hành, việc thi hành luật yếu kém và tham nhũng đã cho phép ngành công nghiệp này tồn tại. Các mạng lưới tội phạm tiếp tục buôn lậu động vật qua các tỉnh, đánh cắp vật nuôi và trốn tránh trách nhiệm.

Việt Nam không thể tự xưng là một quốc gia “văn minh” và tiến bộ trong khi vẫn cho phép hoạt động buôn bán man rợ này tiếp diễn. Thế giới đang theo dõi khi các quốc gia như Hàn Quốc thực hiện các biện pháp quyết liệt để cấm ngành công nghiệp thịt chó. Việt Nam phải làm theo, không chỉ vì lợi ích của động vật mà còn vì sức khỏe, an toàn và nhân phẩm của người dân.

Chúng tôi yêu cầu:

1. Cấm hoàn toàn việc buôn bán thịt chó và mèo trên toàn quốc, kèm theo các hình phạt nghiêm khắc đối với những ai vi phạm.
2. Thực thi nghiêm ngặt các luật hiện hành, bao gồm các chiến dịch trấn áp buôn lậu, giết mổ và bán chó mèo làm thịt.
3. Hỗ trợ các chương trình chuyển đổi để giúp người lao động trong ngành này chuyển sang các nghề nghiệp nhân đạo và bền vững.
4. Các chiến dịch giáo dục cộng đồng nhằm nâng cao nhận thức về sự tàn ác của ngành này và những rủi ro mà nó gây ra cho sức khỏe cộng đồng.

Đã đến lúc hành động. Việt Nam phải xứng đáng với tiềm năng của mình như một quốc gia nhân ái và tiến bộ.


Thân ái,



Đội ngũ @HallieForAnimals
contact@hallieforanimals.org


To whom it may concern,

We write to you as global citizens, animal advocates, and concerned individuals to demand an immediate and total ban on Vietnam’s dog and cat meat trade. This cruel and outdated industry not only inflicts unimaginable suffering on millions of animals but also threatens public health, undermines Vietnam’s international reputation, and contradicts the values of a modern, compassionate society.

- Over six million dogs and one million cats are brutally slaughtered in Vietnam every year. Most of these animals are stolen pets or community animals, torn from their homes and families, only to face horrific conditions, cramped in cages, starved, and subjected to brutal slaughter methods.
- Vietnamese citizens overwhelmingly reject this trade. A 2021 survey by FOUR PAWS found that 91% of Vietnamese believe the trade should be banned or discouraged, and 95% say it is not part of Vietnamese culture. Cities like Hanoi are already taking steps to phase out dog meat consumption, proving that change is possible and desired.
- The trade operates largely outside the law. Despite existing regulations, enforcement is weak, and corruption allows the industry to persist. Criminal networks continue to traffic animals across provinces, stealing pets and evading accountability.

Vietnam cannot claim to be a “civilized” and forward-thinking nation while allowing this barbaric trade to continue. The world is watching as countries like South Korea take decisive action to ban the dog meat industry. Vietnam must follow suit, not just for the sake of animals but for the health, safety, and dignity of its people.

We demand:

1. A nationwide ban on the dog and cat meat trade, with strict penalties for those who violate it.
2. Strong enforcement of existing laws, including crackdowns on illegal trafficking, slaughter, and sale of dogs and cats for meat.
3. Support for transition programs to help workers in the trade move to humane and sustainable livelihoods.
4. Public education campaigns to raise awareness about the cruelty of the trade and the risks it poses to public health.

The time for action is now. Vietnam must live up to its potential as a compassionate and progressive nation.


Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

In Vietnam, an estimated 6 million dogs and 1 million cats are slaughtered for meat every year. Animals are stolen from the streets and from the homes of families, pets ripped from their owners' gardens, still wearing their collars. They're transported for hours or days in wire cages, without food or water, piled on top of one another. They're killed by electrocution, by bludgeoning, and by throat-cutting, often while fully conscious.
The dog and cat meat trade isn't a controlled industry; it operates in the open, in markets and restaurants, largely unchallenged by law. Despite growing opposition from younger Vietnamese generations and repeated calls from international animal welfare organisations, the Vietnamese government has failed to act. Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City have issued non-binding requests to end the trade, but without legislation, they're meaningless.
The trade is a significant driver of rabies and cholera outbreaks, posing a direct public health risk to both Vietnamese citizens and the millions of tourists who visit each year. TNVR programs have proven effective in managing stray populations and controlling the spread of disease, but it's more profitable to steal, cage, and kill.
Vietnam's tourism industry generated over $23 billion in 2024 and is growing fast. Boycott Vietnam until its government acts. Stop purchasing Vietnamese goods, and redirect your travel money to countries that don't profit from the suffering of companion animals.

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

We are writing on behalf of thousands of concerned citizens, animal advocates, and taxpayers who are demanding immediate and meaningful accountability from the leadership of Los Angeles County and the City of Los Angeles regarding the ongoing crisis of animal abuse and neglect taking place in plain sight across the region.

On Skid Row, the situation has reached a level of cruelty that is no longer ignorable. Dogs are confined in wire crates sweltering beneath plastic tarps in the midday heat without food or water. Others limp through trash-strewn streets with open wounds and protruding ribs. Volunteers on the ground have documented dogs being used to test drugs for fentanyl lethality, with several animals dying from overdoses as a result. Pregnant dogs give birth on the streets without medical care. Animals are tied up, tangled in ropes, crammed into tiny cages for days, beaten, and left in the sun without shade. These documented cases have been filmed and reported repeatedly by frontline rescue organizations who have been sounding the alarm for years.

Beyond Skid Row, the crisis extends across the county. In San Fernando, a pet sitter allegedly strangled a 22-month-old American Bully named Chula while her owners were away. In La Verne, a man allegedly beat his family's elderly corgi-chihuahua mix, Hope, to death with a crowbar because her barking disturbed his sleep. In another case, a man allegedly dropped a bulldog named Adriana on her head, kicked her, and threw her into a stack of tires, where she was left to die. These are symptoms of a county in which the message, intentionally or not, is that cruelty carries no real consequences.

When advocates call the police, they are told to call animal control. When animal control is called, they are told to call the police. Calls to the Mayor's office, LA Animal Services, and the LAPD to report dogs being beaten, starved, neglected, and abandoned typically go unanswered. In November 2025, Mayor Karen Bass announced a dedicated task force to address animal cruelty on Skid Row. After a single highly-publicized bust, advocates report they never saw evidence of the task force again, with officers recorded stating the program was disbanded after just a couple of trainings.

Los Angeles rules dictate that the issuance of new breeding licences be suspended when animal shelters exceed 75% capacity, a threshold the city has been well over for years, with shelters currently running at more than double their intended capacity. Meanwhile, on Skid Row, dogs are openly bred and sold in plain sight, with enforcement virtually non-existent. Mayor Bass has proposed cutting millions from the already stretched LA Animal Services department and laying off 62 of its employees, cuts that, according to the department's own interim general manager, would force the closure of at least three of the city's six shelters, in a system that is already overcrowded, understaffed, and euthanizing animals at a historic rate.

Let us be clear about what the taxpayers of Los Angeles are funding. Mayor Karen Bass draws an annual salary of approximately $301,000. Each of the five members of the LA County Board of Supervisors earns $244,727 per year, a collective salary bill for that body alone of over $1.2 million annually. These are the people elected and paid to govern this city and county. For that level of public investment, the very least Angelenos, and indeed a watching world, should expect is the basic enforcement of laws that already exist. California Penal Code 597 prohibits animal cruelty. The laws are written. The budgets are allocated. The salaries are paid. What is absent is the will to act.

We demand the following:

1. Real, sustained enforcement on Skid Row and across LA County, not press releases, not pilot programs that vanish after one action, but a permanent, properly resourced unit with the authority and mandate to investigate, seize animals in danger, and refer cases for prosecution. Results must be measurable and publicly reported.

2. Immediate reversal of proposed cuts to LA Animal Services and a commitment to increase, not reduce, staffing and resources at a time when shelters are overwhelmed, and animals across the county are dying from neglect.

3. Consistent prosecution under California Penal Code 597, regardless of ZIP code or housing status. Cruelty is cruelty. The law does not make exceptions, and neither should those paid to enforce it.

4. Transparent, publicly accessible reporting on animal cruelty complaints, response times, enforcement actions, and outcomes across the county, so that residents can hold you accountable for the results, not just the announcements.

5. Use of your public platforms to make unambiguously clear that animal cruelty in Los Angeles will not be tolerated, and that those responsible will face real legal consequences.

The suffering taking place on the streets of this city is not a secret. It is filmed daily, reported by credible news outlets, documented by rescue volunteers, and witnessed by thousands. The question is no longer whether it is happening. The question is why those being paid hundreds of thousands of dollars in public funds are allowing it to continue.

We are watching. We are organized. And we will not stop until the animals of Los Angeles County receive the protection they deserve are owed under the law.

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

La situación afecta a un perro pequeño perteneciente al apartamento E304. Según varios vecinos, el animal es dejado completamente solo durante todo el día y toda la noche, de forma repetida y continuada, durante un período prolongado. Esto constituye un caso de negligencia continuada, que causa sufrimiento al animal y viola la Ley de Tenencia Responsable de Mascotas y Animales de Compañía de Chile (Ley 21.020).

Este asunto ya ha sido puesto en conocimiento de la administración del condominio y denunciado formalmente ante los Carabineros, pero hasta la fecha no se han implementado soluciones efectivas ni concretas. Los residentes están cada vez más preocupados por el bienestar del perro y solicitan la intervención inmediata del municipio.

- Realizar una inspección inmediata in situ del apartamento E304 para verificar las condiciones de vida del perro  
- Confirmar la identidad del propietario o propietarios responsables y evaluar si el animal está siendo cuidado adecuadamente  
- Garantizar que el perro reciba de inmediato los cuidados adecuados, incluyendo comida, agua, refugio y cualquier atención veterinaria necesaria  
- Aplicar todas las medidas coercitivas pertinentes previstas en la legislación chilena para evitar un mayor abandono o negligencia   

Gracias por su pronta atención a este urgente asunto de bienestar animal.

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

We're writing to formally raise the alarm regarding the welfare of greyhounds being kept in what can only be described as deplorable conditions at a location near Parteen, County Clare. Video evidence has been recorded documenting these conditions, including dogs without access to water and, critically, at least one dog wearing a muzzle, physically preventing it from drinking even if water were available. This isn't a matter of opinion, it's documented suffering.

What's deeply troubling isn't only the condition of these animals, but the institutional failure surrounding them:

— Two inspectors from Greyhound Racing Ireland visited the site and deemed conditions acceptable. This is an organisation with a direct financial interest in the greyhound racing industry. It should never have been in the position of conducting welfare checks in the first place. This is a textbook conflict of interest.

— DAFM and the NCPCA have declined to get involved.

— An Garda Síochána also deemed the conditions acceptable, and rather than investigate the welfare of suffering animals, they're instead pursuing a warrant to identify the individual who recorded the footage, with a view to charging them with trespassing.

If a child were found in equivalent conditions, no water, restrained from drinking, confined without adequate care, no authority in the civilized world would prosecute the person who filmed it. The act of exposure would be considered courageous, not criminal. These animals deserve no less consideration.

Ireland positions itself as a nation of animal lovers. And yet, it appears that as long as an animal generates revenue, its suffering is treated as acceptable collateral. Wales and Scotland have both moved to ban greyhound racing precisely because of the systemic neglect and abuse that accompanies the industry. Ireland must now ask itself what kind of nation it wishes to be.

We are calling on you to:

1. Ensure an independent welfare inspection is conducted immediately at the location near Parteen, Co. Clare, by a body with no financial ties to the greyhound racing industry.
2. Halt any legal proceedings against the individual who recorded the footage. Whistleblowers exposing animal cruelty should be protected, not prosecuted.
3. Launch an urgent review into the conflict of interest inherent in GRI conducting welfare inspections on racing greyhounds.
4. Consider legislative action in line with Wales and Scotland, where greyhound racing has been banned due to endemic welfare failures.

These animals cannot speak. We must.

We expect a public statement response, and we expect action.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1T2tFLsdH4UoGtQCZrYrXBK9PFvRxawSp/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

إلى من يهمه الأمر،

نكتب إليكم على وجه السرعة بخصوص حادثة تم تسجيلها وتداولها عبر الإنترنت، تظهر فيها مراهقان يعلقان قطة حية من أرجلها الأمامية، وهما يحملان أسلحة بيضاء وأدوات بستنة، ويتحدثان عن قتل الحيوان وأكله. ولم يتم بعد تأكيد الموقع الدقيق للحادثة داخل العراق.

نطلب مساعدتكم بكل احترام في:
1. تحديد هوية الأفراد المتورطين
2. ضمان إجراء فحوصات رعاية لأي حيوانات في رعايتهم أو في منازلهم
3. إحالة القاصرين وعائلاتهم إلى خدمات الدعم الاجتماعي أو النفسي المناسبة

هذه ليست مجرد مسألة تتعلق برعاية الحيوانات. إنها مشكلة موثقة تتعلق بالسلامة العامة ونمو الطفل.

التقاليد الإسلامية واضحة تمامًا في هذا الشأن. فقد حذر النبي محمد (صلى الله عليه وسلم) قائلاً: ”في الخير الذي يُعمل به في أي كائن حي أجر“ (البخاري ومسلم)، وقد وثق العلماء أن القسوة المتعمدة على الحيوانات (الإيذاء بالحيوان) تعتبر حرامًا. وقد أشار ابن القيم وغيره من العلماء الكلاسيكيين إلى أن قسوة القلب تجاه المخلوقات هي علامة على الفساد الأخلاقي الذي يمتد إلى العلاقات الإنسانية.

ويدعم ذلك البحث الجنائي الحديث الذي لا يقتصر أصله على الغرب:

• تم توثيق الصلة التي أطلق عليها ”ثلاثية ماكدونالد“ بين القسوة على الحيوانات في مرحلة الطفولة والعنف بين الأشخاص في مرحلة لاحقة، وذلك في دراسات أجريت عبر ثقافات ونظم قانونية متعددة، بما في ذلك أبحاث نُشرت في المجلة العربية للطب النفسي ومراجعات إقليمية في علم الجريمة.

• وجدت دراسة أجريت عام 2015 في مجلة العنف بين الأشخاص (ساهم باحثون من مصر ولبنان في البيانات الإقليمية) أن القسوة على الحيوانات في مرحلة المراهقة كانت من بين أقوى المؤشرات المبكرة على ارتكاب جرائم عنيفة في مرحلة البلوغ.

• اعترف مكتب الأمم المتحدة المعني بالمخدرات والجريمة (UNODC)، وهو هيئة يشارك فيها العراق، رسمياً بالقسوة على الحيوانات كمؤشر مبكر في أطر عمل الوقاية من العنف بين الشباب.

التدخل المبكر لا يحمي الحيوانات فحسب، بل يحمي المجتمع وأسر هؤلاء الأطفال والأطفال أنفسهم.

نطلب بكل احترام من وزارة الداخلية:

• مراجعة اللقطات المتاحة والمساعدة في تحديد الموقع الجغرافي أو الهوية
• توجيه الشرطة المحلية أو الخدمات الاجتماعية لزيارة الأسرة
• ترتيب إخراج أي حيوانات معرضة لخطر المزيد من الأذى
• ربط الأحداث بالدعم النفسي أو الأسري بدلاً من التدابير العقابية وحدها — تظهر الأبحاث باستمرار أن التدخل المبكر أكثر فعالية بكثير

شكراً لاهتمامكم بهذا الأمر.

To whom it may concern,

We write to you with urgency regarding a recorded incident circulating online in which two adolescent males are shown suspending a live cat by its forelimbs, holding bladed weapons and gardening tools, and discussing killing and consuming the animal. The precise location within Iraq hasn't yet been confirmed.

We respectfully request your assistance in:
1. Identifying the individuals involved
2. Ensuring welfare checks on any animals in their care or household
3. Referring the juveniles and their families to appropriate social or psychological support services

This isn't just an animal welfare issue. It's a documented public safety and child development concern.

Islamic tradition is unambiguous on this point. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) warned: "There is a reward for serving any living being" (Bukhari & Muslim), and scholars have documented that deliberate cruelty to animals (al-itha'a bil-hayawan) is considered haram. Ibn al-Qayyim and other classical scholars noted that hardness of heart toward creatures is a sign of moral corruption that extends to human relationships.

This is supported by modern criminological research that is not exclusively Western in origin:

• The "Macdonald Triad" link between childhood animal cruelty and later interpersonal violence is documented in studies conducted across multiple cultures and legal systems, including research published in the Arab Journal of Psychiatry and regional criminology reviews.

• A 2015 study in the Journal of Interpersonal Violence (researchers from Egypt and Lebanon contributed to the regional data) found that animal cruelty in adolescence was among the strongest early predictors of violent offending in adulthood.

• The United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), a body Iraq participates in, has formally recognised animal cruelty as a precursor indicator in youth violence prevention frameworks.

Early intervention protects not only animals but the community, the families of these children, and the children themselves.

We respectfully ask that the Ministry of Interior:

• Review the available footage and assist in geolocation or identification
• Direct local police or social services to visit the household
• Arrange removal of any animals at risk of further harm
• Connect the juveniles with psychological or family support rather than punitive measures alone — research consistently shows early intervention is far more effective

Thank you for your attention to this matter.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/14h1iELuoaEEXeJ7gpJhlbRacvB1oME9K/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team

links.description:
PUBLIC SERVICE ANNOUNCEMENT❗

Tanya at @grandmasbarnrescueandsanctuary has been misrepresenting the care of a dog named Hatchi.

Nearly a year ago, Hatchi was rescued and placed with a foster in Northern California. When that foster could no longer continue due to serious personal circumstances, Tanya stated she would move Hatchi into a safe, loving foster home.

That did not happen.

Hatchi was (until recently) being kept at K9 De Baja, a boarding facility in Tijuana with reviews accusing them of neglect and abuse, while the rescue continued to advertise him on Petfinder as being in a “loving foster home.” This is misleading to the public and unfair to potential adopters and supporters.

Hatchi also has medical needs involving his eye and should not have been sitting in boarding, he needed consistent, hands-on care in a real home.

It's been confirmed that another dog, Zeus, who was pulled by this rescue around a year ago, was in the same situation.

This is not an isolated issue. There is a pattern of:
• Dogs being placed in boarding instead of foster homes
• Fosters not being supported or reimbursed
• Misrepresentation of where and how dogs are being cared for

Even more concerning, when these issues are brought forward, they are denied or redirected instead of being addressed with transparency.

Rescue work requires honesty, accountability, and putting the dogs first, not misleading the public.

Hatchi AND Zeus deserved better.

#Nevada #Sparks #animallover

This operation, run by Kyambadde Ramathan and Ssekidde Charles, is using a classic decoy: they registered LUSWA ANIMAL SANCTUARY (U) LTD as a plain Company with URSB number 80034854234246 on 9 July 2025.
That’s just a company filing, it is NOT a registered charity or NGO. They have zero operating permit from Uganda’s National Bureau for Non-Governmental Organisations. Yet posts and GoFundMes claim they are “a legal, fully registered shelter.”
They’ve successfully convinced a genuine U.S. 501(c)3 to publicly partner with them, sending money for food, carts, and “cancer” treatments while calling Luswa dogs “our rescue partners in Uganda.” That American credibility is the main thing keeping donations flowing.
Meanwhile, the same dogs are recycled across their accounts with fresh “cancer/TVT” stories, starvation emergencies, and urgent surgery appeals.

All accounts involved:

Instagram: @luswa_animalsanctuary (Kyambadde Ramathan)
Instagram: @luswa_animal_sanctuary256 (Ssekidde Charles)
TikTok: @luswaanimalsanctu

They post endless emotional videos while using livestock Taktic (amitraz) on dogs, a product that is never safe or approved for canines.
Do NOT donate.
This is not a sanctuary. It’s a donation funnel built on recycled animals and false legitimacy.
Report the accounts for scams and false information.
Real rescues don’t need to hide behind a company registration and a fooled 501(c)3.

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing as a concerned citizen and animal advocate regarding the ongoing investigation into the alleged animal abuse at Plum Creek Canines in Dickinson, North Dakota. The graphic video that has circulated widely on social media clearly shows an individual (identified publicly as business owner and trainer Neveah Baranko) repeatedly striking and kicking a dog named Bella during what appears to be a training or handling session.

I understand that the Stark County Sheriff’s Office has already conducted interviews, gathered evidence, and forwarded a formal report citing a violation of North Dakota Century Code 36-21.2. I also understand that, after review, your office has appropriately recused itself due to a conflict of interest and has referred the matter to another independent State’s Attorney’s Office for any potential charging decision.

Given the clear video evidence and the fact that this occurred at a licensed dog daycare and training business that serves the public, I respectfully urge your office to ensure that the reviewing prosecutor throws the book at the individual responsible and pursues the strongest possible charges and penalties available under North Dakota law. Animal abuse is not a minor infraction, it is a serious crime that demands full accountability.

There are far too many abusive trainers and kennel operators across the country who continue to harm animals behind closed doors. Strong prosecution in this high-visibility case would send a powerful message of deterrence to others in the industry and help restore public trust that North Dakota will not tolerate cruelty, especially when it involves animals entrusted to “professionals.”

I kindly request a public statement updating the status of the referral, the name of the receiving State’s Attorney’s Office if it can be shared, and any timeline for a charging decision. The community is watching closely and stands ready to support full enforcement of our animal protection laws.

Thank you for your time and for your commitment to justice in this matter.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1yWP1c6MwDRCvGiCxoDtTSvts4ZnwtBrQ/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team

إلى من يهمه الأمر،

نكتب إليكم على وجه السرعة بخصوص حادثة تم تصويرها بالفيديو وتنتشر حاليًا على مواقع التواصل الاجتماعي في مصر. يُظهر الفيديو كلبًا مربوطًا إلى شجرة يتعرض للضرب المتكرر على رأسه بعصا على يد شخصين في قرية النويرات، منطقة العسرات، محافظة سوهاج. وقد تم الكشف عن هوية الجناة علنًا، وهم محمد محمود سعد وآخرون من عائلة الزهراوي. وقد أثار الحادث غضبًا واسع النطاق بين جماعات رعاية الحيوانات المصرية.

نطلب بكل احترام مساعدة وزارة الداخلية ومكتب المدعي العام والسلطات المحلية المعنية في:

1. التحقق من هويات جميع الأفراد المتورطين في الحادث وتحديد أماكنهم.  
2. إجراء عمليات تفتيش فورية على حالة أي حيوانات في رعايتهم أو في منازلهم.  
3. الترتيب لنقل أي حيوانات معرضة لخطر التعرض لمزيد من الأذى.  
4. محاسبة الجناة وفقًا للقانون المصري.

هذه القضية ليست مجرد مسألة رعاية للحيوانات؛ إنها مسألة تتعلق بالسلامة العامة وحماية المجتمع.

الشريعة الإسلامية واضحة جدًا فيما يتعلق بمعاملة الحيوانات. قال النبي محمد، صلى الله عليه وسلم: «كل دابة لها كبد رطب، ولها أجر» (رواه البخاري ومسلم). وقد أشار علماء مثل ابن القيم إلى أن تعذيب الحيوانات عمدًا (القسوة على الحيوانات) محظور، وأن القسوة تجاه المخلوقات هي علامة على الفساد الأخلاقي الذي قد يمتد إلى العلاقات الإنسانية. اللطف مع الحيوانات له أجر، والقسوة عليها هي ذنب جسيم.

علاوة على ذلك، فإن الأفعال المتكررة من القسوة تجاه الكلاب، مثل تقييدها وضربها، تتسبب في إصابة الحيوانات بخوف شديد من البشر. غالبًا ما يجعل هذا الخوف الكلاب أكثر دفاعية وعدوانية عندما يقترب منها أي شخص، مما يزيد بشكل مباشر من خطر هجمات الكلاب على أفراد المجتمع والأطفال والمارة. وبالتالي، فإن مثل هذه الأفعال تعرض السلامة العامة للخطر بدلاً من حمايتها.

نطلب بكل احترام من وزارة الداخلية والنيابة العامة:

- مراجعة الفيديو المتاح والمساعدة في التحقق من الهويات والموقع الجغرافي.  
- توجيه مركز شرطة العاصرة في سوهاج لزيارة المنزل وإجراء تحقيق شامل.  
- الترتيب لإخراج أي حيوانات معرضة لخطر الإساءة.  
- اتخاذ جميع الإجراءات القانونية اللازمة لمحاسبة المسؤولين.

To whom it may concern,

We write to you with urgency regarding a recorded incident currently circulating on social media in Egypt. The footage shows a dog tied to a tree being beaten repeatedly over the head with a stick by two individuals in Al-Nuwayrat village, Al-Asirat center, Sohag governorate. The perpetrators have been publicly identified as Muhammad Mahmoud Saad and others from the Al-Zaharweh family. The video has sparked widespread outrage among Egyptian animal welfare groups.

We respectfully request the assistance of the Ministry of Interior, the Public Prosecution, and relevant local authorities in:

1. Confirming the identities and locating all individuals involved in the incident.  
2. Conducting immediate welfare checks on any animals in their care or household.  
3. Arranging for the removal of any animals at risk of further harm.  
4. Holding the perpetrators accountable under Egyptian law.

This is not merely an animal welfare issue. It is a documented public safety and community protection concern.

Islamic tradition is unambiguous on the treatment of animals. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) stated: “There is a reward for serving any living being” (Bukhari & Muslim). Scholars such as Ibn al-Qayyim have noted that deliberate cruelty to animals (al-itha’a bil-hayawan) is haram and that hardness of heart toward creatures is a sign of moral corruption that can extend to human relationships. Kindness to animals is rewarded, while cruelty is a grave sin.

Additionally, repeated acts of cruelty toward dogs — such as tying them up and beating them — cause the animals to develop intense fear of humans. This fear often leads dogs to become more defensive and aggressive when approached, directly increasing the risk of dog attacks on community members, children, and passersby. Such behavior therefore endangers public safety rather than protecting it.

We respectfully ask the Ministry of Interior and the Public Prosecution to:

- Review the available footage and assist in confirming identities and geolocation.  
- Direct local police in Sohag (Al-Asirat center) to visit the household and conduct a full investigation.  
- Arrange for the removal of any animals at risk of further harm.  
- Take all necessary legal measures to hold those responsible accountable.

We urge swift action to demonstrate that Egypt will not tolerate such acts, in line with both religious values and public safety needs. The Egyptian Public Prosecution has previously emphasized that harming animals is forbidden by religious, ethical, and legal standards.

Thank you for your attention to this matter and for your commitment to protecting both human and animal welfare in society.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1hZK8XR2yF0GcCFn3-ofb3s0vhe5p9LQ3/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,

إلى من يهمه الأمر،

نكتب إليكم على وجه السرعة بخصوص مقطع الفيديو الذي انتشر على نطاق واسع من قرية النويرات، مركز العاصرات، محافظة سوهاج. يُظهر المقطع عدة أشخاص وهم يربطون كلبًا بشجرة ويضربونه بوحشية حتى الموت بعصا خشبية. وقد تم الكشف عن هوية الجناة علنًا، وهم محمد محمود سعد وأفراد آخرون من عائلة الزهروة.

ونثني بصدق على وزارة الداخلية وقوات الأمن لسرعة اعتقال الأشخاص الخمسة المتورطين. ويحظى هذا الاستجابة السريعة بتقدير كبير من قبل المدافعين عن رعاية الحيوانات في جميع أنحاء مصر.

ومع ذلك، فإن الاعتقال وحده لا يكفي. ونحث الآن النيابة العامة بكل احترام على المضي قدماً فوراً في الإجراءات القانونية الكاملة والسعي إلى توقيع أقسى عقوبة ممكنة بموجب القانون المصري.

أفادت التقارير أن المشتبه بهم اعترفوا بارتكاب الفعل، مدعين أنهم خشوا أن يكون الكلب مصابًا بداء الكلب وقد يؤذي أطفالهم. ورغم أننا نتفهم قلق الجمهور بشأن داء الكلب، فإن ربط حيوان بشجرة وضربه حتى الموت ليس رد فعل مقبولًا أو قانونيًا. فهناك سلطات بيطرية وصحية مختصة لمثل هذه الحالات. كان هذا فعلًا واضحًا ومتعمدًا ينطوي على قسوة شديدة وأثار غضبًا عامًا واسع النطاق.

نطلب بكل احترام من النيابة العامة والسلطات المعنية ما يلي:

1. الإسراع في التحقيق وإحالة القضية إلى المحكمة دون تأخير.  
2. محاكمة جميع الأفراد الخمسة الذين تم تحديد هويتهم بأقصى ما يسمح به القانون (بما في ذلك المشتبه به الموجود حالياً في الخارج).  
3. السعي إلى الحصول على أقصى عقوبة رادعة لإرسال رسالة واضحة مفادها أن مثل هذه الأفعال التي تنطوي على القسوة تجاه الحيوانات لن يتم التسامح معها في مصر.  
4. ضمان رفاهية أي حيوانات أخرى في المنزل وإبعادها عن الخطر إذا لزم الأمر.

هذه ليست مجرد مسألة تتعلق برفاهية الحيوانات — إنها قضية تتعلق بالسلامة العامة والأخلاق. القسوة المتكررة والشديدة تجاه الحيوانات يمكن أن تشير إلى مشاكل أعمق قد تعرض المجتمع ككل للخطر. التقاليد الإسلامية واضحة جدًا في هذا الشأن: قال النبي محمد (صلى الله عليه وسلم): «في الخير من خدمة أي كائن حي أجر» (البخاري ومسلم). تعتبر القسوة المتعمدة تجاه الحيوانات خطيئة جسيمة وعلامة على الفساد الأخلاقي.

نحثكم على إظهار أن مصر تأخذ القسوة تجاه الحيوانات على محمل الجد من خلال ضمان المقاضاة السريعة والعقوبة الصارمة في هذه القضية. سيؤدي مثل هذا الإجراء أيضًا إلى تعزيز الدعم العام لقانون حماية الحيوانات الذي طال انتظاره والذي يطالب به العديد من المصريين.

نشكركم على اهتمامكم بهذه المسألة وعلى التزامكم بالعدالة وحماية رفاهية الإنسان والحيوان على حد سواء.

دليل بالفيديو: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1c50rkz7wNAGvGOvCkWJOfZPQj-71qjAk/view?usp=sharing

مع خالص التقدير،

To whom it may concern,

We write to you with urgency regarding the widely circulated video from Al-Nuwayrat village, Al-Asirat Center, Sohag Governorate. The footage shows several individuals tying a dog to a tree and brutally beating it to death with a wooden stick. The perpetrators have been publicly identified as Muhammad Mahmoud Saad and other members of the Al-Zaharweh family.

We sincerely commend the Ministry of Interior and the security forces for the swift arrests of the five individuals involved. This rapid response is greatly appreciated by animal welfare advocates across Egypt.

However, an arrest alone is not enough. We now respectfully urge the Public Prosecution Office to move forward immediately with full legal proceedings and to seek the strongest possible punishment under Egyptian law.

The suspects have reportedly confessed to the act, claiming they feared the dog had rabies and might harm their children. While we understand public concern over rabies, tying an animal to a tree and beating it to death is not an acceptable or lawful response. Proper veterinary and health authorities exist for such situations. This was a clear and deliberate act of extreme cruelty that has caused widespread public outrage.

We respectfully request the Public Prosecution and relevant authorities to:

1. Expedite the investigation and refer the case to court without delay.  
2. Prosecute all five identified individuals to the fullest extent of the law (including the suspect currently abroad).  
3. Seek the maximum deterrent sentence to send a clear message that such acts of animal cruelty will not be tolerated in Egypt.  
4. Ensure the welfare of any other animals in the household and remove them from risk if necessary.

This is not only an animal welfare matter — it is a public safety and moral issue. Repeated extreme cruelty toward animals can signal deeper problems that may endanger the wider community. Islamic tradition is very clear on this: the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, “There is a reward for serving any living being” (Bukhari & Muslim). Deliberate cruelty to animals is considered a grave sin and a sign of moral corruption.

We urge you to demonstrate that Egypt takes animal cruelty seriously by ensuring swift prosecution and a firm punishment in this case. Such action will also strengthen public support for the long-awaited animal protection law that many Egyptians are calling for.

Thank you for your attention to this matter and for your commitment to justice and the protection of both human and animal welfare.

Sincerely,

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing to demand an immediate welfare check, seizure of all animals, criminal charges, and a permanent ban on animal ownership/exhibition for Joseph Louis Ramos, also known as Joseph Ramos-Noal, Joseph Noal, or Joseph Noah.

Mr. Ramos has been publicly displaying a rotating "Noah's Ark" menagerie of live dogs, cats, guinea pigs, rabbits, and birds on sidewalks in Manhattan (recently Union Square and Columbus Circle/59th Street Metro Station entrance) for over 25 years. He transports the animals in crates via subway and solicits donations while they remain almost completely immobile.

Recent and ongoing evidence of severe neglect includes:
- A visibly emaciated cat showing clear signs of long-term neglect, including terrible coat quality, a wide hind-leg stance while eating (indicating pain), pecking at seeds like a bird, and paying no mind to the birds around it (despite cats being obligate carnivores and natural hunters).
- Multiple animals appearing comatose, "zombie-like," or in induced tonic immobility, unresponsive to traffic, noise, petting, or other animals, consistent with long-term sedation, starvation, or extreme stress.

Complaints date back to at least 2011, with detailed exposés in 2017 and 2021 documenting the exact same pattern. Activists have repeatedly contacted the NYPD, ASPCA, and NYC Health Department, yet Mr. Ramos continues operating without the required NYC Health Code permit for public animal exhibitions (Sec. 161.01). To whom it may concern,

I am writing to report ongoing animal neglect at 1804 Prairie Town Way, Roseville, CA 95747.

Two dogs have been kept locked inside a non-climate-controlled garage 24/7 for over a year, exposed to extreme heat and cold with no temperature control or relief. I respectfully request an immediate welfare check, full investigation, removal of the dogs if necessary, and appropriate enforcement action against the owner.

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing to demand immediate accountability following a clear case of animal abuse and multiple city agency failures.

Recently, on East 28th Street between 1st and 2nd Avenues in Manhattan, a woman was observed beating her dog after it vomited on the street. The terrified dog urinated itself in fear. Despite multiple calls, NYPD officers took over an hour to respond. The dog was removed and taken to Animal Care Centers of NYC (ACC), yet was later released back to the same abuser. This woman is already known to local hospitals for mental health issues and has declined offered help.

This incident highlights two critical failures:
1: Unacceptably slow NYPD response to animal cruelty calls.
2: ACC’s decision to return a clearly abused animal to a known abuser despite available evidence and the owner’s documented mental health concerns.

New York City cannot claim to be progressive while allowing dogs to be handfed to abusers.

I respectfully request:

1: An immediate investigation into this specific case, including retrieval of the dog if it remains in danger.
2: A full review and reform of ACC policies on returning animals to individuals with histories of abuse or untreated mental health issues.
3: Improved NYPD training and response protocols for animal cruelty calls to ensure timely intervention.
4: Better inter-agency coordination between NYPD, ACC, and mental health services to protect animals and support vulnerable owners.

The public is watching, and we expect real change to prevent this from happening again.
Thank you for your urgent attention to this matter.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1d7RL3t3mSgxZrijkje6dGWYqHuqKQ5ar/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing to formally report an act of animal cruelty witnessed on the morning of April 14, 2026, at 4 Seasons Carwash, Cornwall, Ontario.

A dog was physically abused by its owner, who was recorded dragging the dog and physically striking it.
Prior to the recording, the owner was seen removing his belt, striking the ground near the dog with it, screaming at the dog, and lifting the dog off the ground by its collar.
When concerned witnesses intervened, the owner responded with aggression and stated, "It's my dog, I'll do what I want with it."

We respectfully demand the following immediate actions:

1: Obtain and preserve CCTV footage from 4 Seasons Carwash and nearby businesses for the morning of April 14, 2026.
2: Identify the perpetrator using available video, witness descriptions, and business records.
3: Remove the dog from the owner's custody pending a full welfare assessment under Ontario's Provincial Animal Welfare Services (PAWS) Act.
4: Lay appropriate charges under the PAWS Act, Criminal Code of Canada (s. 445.1), and/or Cornwall's Animal Control By-law.

Research consistently shows a strong link between animal abuse, domestic violence, and child abuse. Individuals who abuse animals in public with an attitude of entitlement and control ("It's my dog, I'll do what I want") often escalate violence behind closed doors. If this individual is willing to assault a defenseless animal in full view of witnesses, what is occurring with vulnerable family members, partners, children, or other dependents, in private?

This is not just an animal welfare issue; it is a community safety issue.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/16OWISrRcKOLgruQKmb0scwa1xwJHUB1K/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

A quien corresponda:

Les escribo como ciudadano preocupado para dar seguimiento al grave caso de maltrato animal ocurrido el 20 de abril de 2026 en el apartamento 108 del Condominio Cumbres de Hualpén (Cristóbal Colón 8551).

Tengo entendido que la PDI BIDEMA está llevando a cabo una investigación y que la Municipalidad de Hualpén ha presentado una querella, habiéndose retirado a los tres perros del lugar. Si bien se agradecen estas medidas iniciales, insto respetuosamente a que se tomen las siguientes acciones inmediatas y decisivas:

1: La localización y detención inmediatas del autor identificado, Jorge Iván Muñoz Carvajal (RUT 13.382.743-9), por el lanzamiento violento y el maltrato de los perros que les causó fracturas y lesiones graves en la espalda.
2: La prohibición permanente de devolver cualquiera de los tres perros a esta persona, colocándolos en su lugar bajo custodia protectora o en hogares de acogida o de adopción adecuados para garantizar su seguridad.
3: El enjuiciamiento completo en toda la extensión de la ley en virtud de la Ley 21.020 (Tenencia Responsable de Mascotas y Animales de Compañía), incluyendo todas las sanciones aplicables, tales como multas, inhabilitación de por vida para tener animales y cualquier sanción privativa de libertad que justifique la gravedad de las lesiones y las pruebas (incluidos los videos de los vecinos y el testimonio de testigos oculares).

Este caso ha provocado una indignación pública generalizada debido a la brutalidad clara y documentada que implica. Es esencial una aplicación firme y rápida de la ley para proteger a los animales, disuadir de futuras infracciones y defender el espíritu de las leyes de protección animal de Chile.

Pruebas en vídeo: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1EBif_GBTcvJ8c_ue8aWj8Gl5XAqSQsCd/view?usp=sharing

Atentamente,



Equipo de @HallieForAnimals

I understand that the PDI BIDEMA is conducting an investigation and that the Municipality of Hualpén has filed a querella, with the three dogs having been removed from the premises. While these initial steps are appreciated, I respectfully urge the following immediate and decisive actions:

1: The immediate location and arrest of the identified perpetrator, Jorge Iván Muñoz Carvajal (RUT 13.382.743-9), for the violent throwing and mistreatment of the dogs that caused fractures and severe back injuries.
2: A permanent prohibition on returning any of the three dogs to this individual, placing them instead in protective custody or suitable foster/adoptive homes to ensure their safety.

This case has caused widespread public outrage due to the clear and documented brutality involved. Strong and swift enforcement is essential to protect the animals, deter future offenses, and uphold the intent of Chile’s animal protection laws.

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing as a concerned citizen demanding the immediate release and rehoming of the approximately 2,000 beagles still confined at Ridglan Farms in Blue Mounds, Wisconsin.

In 2025, a Dane County Circuit Court judge found probable cause that Ridglan Farms committed felony animal cruelty violations and explicitly noted that District Attorney Ismael Ozanne had failed to properly investigate. Rather than pursuing full prosecution, the DA accepted a settlement that allows Ridglan to continue selling dogs to research facilities and conducting on-site research until the breeding license expires on July 1, 2026. This deal leaves hundreds of dogs in potentially abusive conditions for months longer while only minor charges (such as a manure storage violation) have been filed. Over 100 Wisconsin humane societies and rescues have urged the DA to act, yet the response has been inadequate.

Meanwhile, Sheriff Kalvin Barrett’s office has focused its resources on referring criminal charges against activists attempting rescues and using force to protect the facility, rather than prioritizing the welfare of the animals or facilitating their safe removal. The public has made it clear: these dogs deserve homes now, not continued confinement or sale to labs.

Ridglan Farms: Please immediately accept offers from qualified rescues and humane societies to rehome every remaining beagle. Do not wait until the July deadline or sell any more dogs into research.

District Attorney Ozanne and Sheriff Barrett: The time for half-measures and excuses is over. Use your authority to investigate fully, hold Ridglan accountable beyond minor citations, and ensure these dogs are released to loving homes without further delay. With all due respect, it's high time you prioritize protecting and serving the vulnerable and tax-paying public that your department was created for, rather than protecting law-breaking corporate institutions.

The community expects compassion and decisive action, not protection of a facility that has already been found to violate animal cruelty laws.

Thank you for treating this urgent animal welfare crisis with the seriousness it deserves.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1fEvPEOcdZPPSmMFF306lT5IWOS3UM0lC/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing to urgently report a serious incident of animal cruelty combined with criminal intimidation that occurred on the afternoon of 25 April 2026 near Dwarka Sector 11 Metro Station, New Delhi.
A man (appearing intoxicated) forcibly dragged a resisting dog that clearly did not belong to him. When a bystander attempted to intervene and stop the cruelty, the suspect pulled out a knife and threatened him, causing fear and allowing the perpetrator to escape in an e-rickshaw bearing registration number DL6ER5853.

This case involves multiple offences:

1: Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 – Sections 3 and 11 (treating an animal cruelly by subjecting it to unnecessary pain and suffering).
2: IPC Section 506 – Criminal Intimidation (threatening with a knife to cause alarm and deter lawful intervention).
3: Possible additional charges: Theft of the dog, public nuisance, and any other sections applicable based on investigation.

I strongly demand the following immediate actions:

1: Register an FIR/complaint without delay under the relevant sections of the PCA Act and IPC (including Section 506 for the knife threat).
2: Trace the e-rickshaw DL6ER5853 (which operates in Dwarka) and question the driver for critical leads on the suspect’s identity and current location of the dog.
3: Review CCTV footage from Dwarka Sector 11 Metro Station and surrounding areas from the afternoon of 25 April 2026.
4: Locate, rescue the dog immediately, and ensure it receives veterinary care if needed.
5: Apprehend the suspect at the earliest and take strict legal action to deter such incidents of animal cruelty and armed threats in public.
6: Provide a complaint/FIR number and keep the public updated on the progress.

This is a time-sensitive matter involving both animal welfare and public safety.

Thank you for treating this with the highest priority.

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

Following Monday's Westminster Hall debate on e-petition 736578, I am writing as a deeply concerned member of the public to demand immediate action to close MBR Acres in Wyton, Cambridgeshire, revoke its licence, and accelerate the phase-out of dog testing.

I have seen the whistleblower footage from inside MBR Acres showing young beagle puppies being forcibly trained for gavage (pipes forced down their throats) and inhalation mask procedures. Around 2,000 beagles are bred and sold every year from this facility alone for repeated-dose toxicity and inhalation studies in UK labs. Britain claims to be a modern nation, a nation of animal lovers, and yet we actively participate in these barbaric, dark-ages-esque practices. This is not acceptable in 2026.

In yesterday’s debate, Minister Ian Murray stated:
“I look forward to the day when we can finally bring an end to animal testing and the use of dogs in scientific research. Unfortunately, that day is not quite yet with us… Our approach to achieve that is set out in last November’s ‘Replacing animals in science’ strategy… However, for now, the carefully regulated use of animals, including dogs, in scientific research unfortunately remains.”

The “Replacing Animals in Science” strategy is all well and good on paper, but these are just words, where is the urgent action? Labour’s 2024 manifesto commitment to partnering with scientists, industry and civil society to phase out animal testing is showing no meaningful movement, with all due respect: 41% of the 2024 Labour manifesto contents shows no movement, a sales pitch to get into office is not an accurate model of how the Labour Party behaves once in power. Targets for modest reductions by 2030 and waiting until 2035 are far too slow. In the next nine years, how many more thousands of dogs will suffer and die in pointless tests when, as you know, over 90% of drugs that pass animal safety and efficacy trials still fail in humans because beagles and humans have fundamentally different metabolisms, immune systems and biology?

Yet the Government is spending £75 million of taxpayers’ money on a “Replacing Animals in Science” strategy to develop and validate alternatives that already exist. We now have far superior human-relevant technologies: lab-grown human tissues, organoids, and organ-on-a-chip systems. These methods better predict human responses, catch toxicities earlier, and could dramatically accelerate the development of safe cures.

The public will not tolerate this any longer. The footage is public, the scientific failures are documented, and the human-relevant alternatives exist and are superior. It is time to pack this in.

I am calling on you to:

1: Immediately review and revoke MBR Acres’ breeding licence under the Animals (Scientific Procedures) Act 1986.
2: Require the safe rehoming of all dogs currently held there.
3: Accelerate the full phase-out of dog use in regulatory toxicity testing, starting with an outright ban on breeding beagles for this purpose.
4: Deliver on the strong cross-party calls made in Monday's debate by backing Petition 736578, supporting Herbie’s Law, and implementing urgent timelines for replacement with modern methods.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1oz3v-2fBFYrbcdHfbMGjiH2-CAPgxIS3/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,


@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing as a concerned citizen to report a serious and disturbing incident of intentional animal cruelty that deserves immediate media attention and public scrutiny.

This case involves the poisoning of five dogs at a Houston residence and a complete lack of in-person police response despite calls from the owner.

On or around April 23, 2026, someone (believed to be a neighbor) allegedly sprayed pesticide into or across the property lines of the home belonging to Chanice Bonner. The use of this pesticide is strongly indicated by the presence of dead bees found everywhere throughout the yard.
As a direct result of the exposure, five of Chanice Bonner’s dogs were poisoned. One of the dogs, named Mya, was subsequently found dead with blood leaking from her ears, eyes, and mouth, an outcome consistent with severe toxic poisoning.

The owner reported the incident to the Houston Police Department. Despite the clear evidence of a crime having occurred, including the widespread dead bees and the death of Mya, no police officers have ever shown up to the location.
The matter has reportedly been handled only as a delayed phone report with no further action taken.
Neighbors have been identified as possible parties involved and have denied responsibility, yet no formal investigation appears to have been launched to examine the facts, collect evidence, or determine what occurred.

Under Texas law, the intentional administration of poison or any substance that causes serious bodily injury or death to an animal is a criminal offense.

With all due respect, "it's just a dog" doesn't fly here. Animal cruelty is well-documented by law enforcement agencies, including the FBI, as a frequent predictor and co-occurring factor in other serious violent crimes against people. Allowing such an incident to go uninvestigated not only fails the victim but also leaves the broader community at potential risk.

Please treat this case with the urgency and attention it deserves.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1lcfcX-GpCqccJqMlfyFaPBTgeHRRIVR0/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,

links.title: Stop The Cat & Dog Meat Trade in Vietnam
links.mailtoSubject: Việt Nam phải chấm dứt hoạt động buôn bán thịt chó và mèo tàn bạo/Vietnam Must End the Brutal Dog and Cat Meat Trade
links.description:
SEND THE ONE-CLICK EMAIL IN MY LINKTREE TO VIETNAM AUTHORITIES TITLED "STOP THE CAT & DOG MEAT TRADE IN VIETNAM"❗️

These dogs were not saved, the truck wasn't stopped, the police didn't get involved. Because in Vietnam, this is somehow legal.

In Vietnam, an estimated 6 million dogs and 1 million cats are slaughtered for meat every year. Animals are stolen from the streets and from the homes of families, pets ripped from their owners' gardens, still wearing their collars. They're transported for hours or days in wire cages, without food or water, piled on top of one another. They're killed by electrocution, by bludgeoning, and by throat-cutting, often while fully conscious.
The dog and cat meat trade isn't a controlled industry; it operates in the open, in markets and restaurants, largely unchallenged by law. Despite growing opposition from younger Vietnamese generations and repeated calls from international animal welfare organisations, the Vietnamese government has failed to act. Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City have issued non-binding requests to end the trade, but without legislation, they're meaningless.
The trade is a significant driver of rabies and cholera outbreaks, posing a direct public health risk to both Vietnamese citizens and the millions of tourists who visit each year. TNVR programs have proven effective in managing stray populations and controlling the spread of disease, but it's more profitable to steal, cage, and kill.
Vietnam's tourism industry generated over $23 billion in 2024 and is growing fast. Boycott Vietnam until its government acts. Stop purchasing Vietnamese goods, and redirect your travel money to countries that don't profit from the suffering of companion animals.

#vietnam #doglover #endthedogmeattrade

links.mailtoBody:
Kính gửi quý vị,

Chúng tôi viết thư này với tư cách là những công dân toàn cầu, những người bảo vệ động vật và những cá nhân quan tâm, để kêu gọi hành động ngay lập tức và quyết đoán nhằm chấm dứt nạn buôn bán thịt chó và mèo tại Việt Nam. Ngành kinh doanh này gây ra đau khổ vô cùng lớn cho hàng triệu con vật, đặt ra những rủi ro nghiêm trọng cho sức khỏe cộng đồng, và ngày càng mâu thuẫn với các giá trị và khát vọng của chính xã hội Việt Nam.

Quy mô của sự đau khổ là rất lớn. Hơn sáu triệu con chó và một triệu con mèo bị giết mổ tại Việt Nam mỗi năm. Nhiều con trong số đó là thú cưng bị đánh cắp hoặc động vật cộng đồng, bị vận chuyển trong điều kiện tàn nhẫn và bị giết bằng những phương pháp gây ra đau đớn kéo dài.

Điều quan trọng là chính người dân Việt Nam đang dẫn đầu lời kêu gọi thay đổi. Một cuộc khảo sát năm 2021 của tổ chức FOUR PAWS cho thấy 91% người Việt Nam tin rằng nạn buôn bán này nên bị cấm hoặc hạn chế, và 95% cho rằng đây không phải là một phần của văn hóa Việt Nam. Các thành phố như Hà Nội đã đang thực hiện những bước đi có ý nghĩa để loại bỏ việc tiêu thụ thịt chó — cho thấy rằng cải cách vừa khả thi vừa được công chúng ủng hộ.

Nạn buôn bán này cũng phần lớn hoạt động trong vùng xám pháp lý. Mặc dù đã có các quy định hiện hành, việc thực thi vẫn chưa nhất quán, và các mạng lưới tội phạm tiếp tục vận chuyển động vật qua các tỉnh, đánh cắp thú cưng và trốn tránh trách nhiệm.

Việt Nam có cơ hội trở thành quốc gia dẫn đầu khu vực trong vấn đề này. Các quốc gia châu Á — bao gồm Hàn Quốc, nước vừa thông qua lệnh cấm mang tính bước ngoặt đối với ngành thịt chó — đang thực hiện những hành động quyết đoán. Việt Nam có thể và nên đi theo con đường này, vì lợi ích của động vật, sức khỏe cộng đồng và vị thế của đất nước trong cộng đồng quốc tế.

Chúng tôi trân trọng kêu gọi quý cơ quan:

1. Ủng hộ lệnh cấm toàn quốc đối với hoạt động buôn bán thịt chó và mèo, với các hình phạt rõ ràng đối với những hành vi vi phạm.
2. Tăng cường thực thi các luật hiện hành, bao gồm hành động chống lại nạn buôn bán, giết mổ và bán chó mèo lấy thịt trái phép.
3. Tài trợ các chương trình chuyển đổi để hỗ trợ những người lao động trong ngành này chuyển sang các sinh kế nhân đạo và bền vững.
4. Đầu tư vào các chiến dịch giáo dục cộng đồng nhằm nâng cao nhận thức về vấn đề phúc lợi động vật và các rủi ro sức khỏe cộng đồng liên quan đến nạn buôn bán này.

Chúng tôi tin rằng Chính phủ Việt Nam cùng chia sẻ cam kết của chúng tôi về một xã hội nhân ái và hướng tới tương lai. Chúng tôi kính mong quý vị biến cam kết đó thành hành động.

Trân trọng,



Đội ngũ @HallieForAnimals
contact@hallieforanimals.org


To whom it may concern,

We write to you as global citizens, animal advocates, and concerned individuals to urge immediate and decisive action to end Vietnam's dog and cat meat trade. This industry causes immense suffering to millions of animals, poses serious risks to public health, and increasingly conflicts with the values and aspirations of Vietnamese society itself.

The scale of suffering is significant. Over six million dogs and one million cats are slaughtered in Vietnam every year. Many are stolen pets or community animals, transported in cruel conditions and subjected to methods of slaughter that cause prolonged pain and distress.

Critically, Vietnamese citizens themselves are leading the call for change. A 2021 survey by FOUR PAWS found that 91% of Vietnamese people believe the trade should be banned or discouraged, and 95% say it is not part of Vietnamese culture. Cities like Hanoi are already taking meaningful steps to phase out dog meat consumption — demonstrating that reform is both possible and publicly supported.

The trade also operates largely in legal grey areas. Despite existing regulations, enforcement remains inconsistent, and criminal networks continue to traffic animals across provinces, stealing pets and evading accountability.

Vietnam has an opportunity to be a regional leader on this issue. Countries across Asia — including South Korea, which recently passed a landmark ban on the dog meat industry — are taking decisive action. Vietnam can and should follow this path, for the benefit of animals, public health, and its standing in the international community.

We respectfully urge your office to:

1. Support a nationwide ban on the dog and cat meat trade, with clear penalties for violations.
2. Strengthen enforcement of existing laws, including action against illegal trafficking, slaughter, and sale of dogs and cats for meat.
3. Fund transition programmes to support workers in the trade in moving to humane and sustainable livelihoods.
4. Invest in public education campaigns highlighting both the animal welfare concerns and the public health risks associated with the trade.

We believe Vietnam's government shares our commitment to a compassionate and forward-thinking society. We ask you to translate that commitment into action.

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team

These dogs were not saved, the truck wasn't stopped, the police didn't get involved. Because in Vietnam, this is somehow legal.

In Vietnam, an estimated 6 million dogs and 1 million cats are slaughtered for meat every year. Animals are stolen from the streets and from the homes of families, pets ripped from their owners' gardens, still wearing their collars. They're transported for hours or days in wire cages, without food or water, piled on top of one another. They're killed by electrocution, by bludgeoning, and by throat-cutting, often while fully conscious.
The dog and cat meat trade isn't a controlled industry; it operates in the open, in markets and restaurants, largely unchallenged by law. Despite growing opposition from younger Vietnamese generations and repeated calls from international animal welfare organisations, the Vietnamese government has failed to act. Hanoi and Ho Chi Minh City have issued non-binding requests to end the trade, but without legislation, they're meaningless.
The trade is a significant driver of rabies and cholera outbreaks, posing a direct public health risk to both Vietnamese citizens and the millions of tourists who visit each year. TNVR programs have proven effective in managing stray populations and controlling the spread of disease, but it's more profitable to steal, cage, and kill.
Vietnam's tourism industry generated over $23 billion in 2024 and is growing fast. Boycott Vietnam until its government acts. Stop purchasing Vietnamese goods, and redirect your travel money to countries that don't profit from the suffering of companion animals.
