links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

I'm reporting the physical abuse of dogs at The Pet Whispers in Encinitas. This isn't secondhand, the abuse is recorded on video, and that footage is available to your investigators now.

It's been reported that SDHS won't act without a firsthand witness. That is not a real legal barrier. In October 2025, San Diego County opened a cruelty case on a dog based on a recording submitted by a member of the public, took the animal into protective care, and secured a conviction through the DA's Animal Cruelty Prosecution Unit, the offender was barred from owning animals for five years. The evidence in that case was a video from the public. The evidence here is a video from the public. There is no honest reason one was investigated and this one is being waved off.

Physically abusing an animal is a crime under California Penal Code § 597. A recording of that crime is evidence. Refusing to look at evidence because no one will volunteer to stand as a witness is not how any other crime is handled, and it is not how this one should be handled.

I am asking SDHS Humane Law Enforcement to open a case on The Pet Whispers, obtain and preserve the footage, and refer the matter to the DA's Animal Cruelty Prosecution Unit.

Investigate The Pet Whispers now.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_pBw0WxFlkuq6zI-e-6S6xx_ihK5y3QG/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

A one-year-old English Bulldog named Bruce drowned in the pool at Camp Canine, 803 E Montecito Street, while in the facility's paid care. English Bulldogs are poor swimmers prone to sinking, a foreseeable hazard at any boarding facility that operates a pool. Bruce was left unsupervised around that water, no one noticed he was missing, the facility has allegedly attributed this to a shift change, and by the time his owner arrived to collect him, rigor mortis had reportedly set in. He had been dead for a significant period, and no one thought to contact Bruce's owner during that time.

We demand:

1: A formal investigation into the supervision, headcount, and emergency protocols that allowed Bruce to die unnoticed in the facility's care.
2: Referral to the District Attorney to determine whether the neglect meets the threshold under California Penal Code § 597(b).
3: A review of the facility's standing to operate pending the outcome of that investigation.
4: A public statement from the City acknowledging Bruce's death and the action being taken.
4: Full transparency: the findings of the investigation released to the public, not resolved behind closed doors.

A dog died in paid custody from a hazard the facility failed to guard, and no one was watching closely enough to notice he was gone.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1m9gTG-Xu93XkiHtQtv_aizcsVkxqk0K4/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
A quien corresponda:

Les escribimos en relación con un acto de maltrato animal ocurrido en el distrito de Pilar. Federico Mentasti, quien se presenta como etólogo, está acusado de torturar, golpear, ahogar hasta el borde de la muerte, incitar a otros perros a atacarlo y, finalmente, ahorcar a un perro hasta matarlo. Se rescataron cinco perros de la propiedad y se los trasladó al Refugio Soplo de Vida. Estos actos constituyen infracciones a los artículos 1 a 3 de la Ley Nacional 14.346. Tenemos entendido que fue detenido y puesto en libertad poco después, y que los cargos no están claros.

Como ciudadanos y organizaciones que seguimos este caso, exigimos:

1: Una investigación exhaustiva de todos los actos contemplados en la Ley 14.346, incluyendo la incautación y el análisis de todas las pruebas videográficas documentadas.
2: Que su puesta en libertad no dé lugar a que el caso sea archivado o se estanque, y que los cargos reflejen actos de crueldad (art. 3), no un delito menor.
3: Que el caso llegue a juicio y se solicite la pena máxima prevista por la ley.
4: La prohibición de tener animales y la inhabilitación para tener contacto con ellos o cuidarlos.
5: Verificación del estado y bienestar de los cinco perros rescatados en el Refugio Soplo de Vida.
6: Una declaración pública sobre el estado del caso y total transparencia: que se comuniquen públicamente los avances y las resoluciones.

El hecho de que alguien que se presenta como un profesional en comportamiento animal esté acusado de estos actos agrava, y no atenúa, el caso.

Prueba en video: https://drive.google.com/file/d/16yTkN8SAt_plMZAa1xLmyFvmoIlePVK7/view?usp=sharing

Atentamente,



Equipo de @HallieForAnimals
contact@hallieforanimals.org



To whom it may concern,

We write regarding an act of animal cruelty in the Pilar district. Federico Mentasti, who presents himself as an ethologist, is accused of torturing, beating, drowning to the brink of death, setting other dogs upon, and finally hanging a dog to death. Five dogs were removed from the property and taken to Refugio Soplo de Vida. These acts fall under Articles 1–3 of National Law 14.346. We understand he was arrested and released soon after, and that the charges are unclear.

As citizens and organizations following this case, we demand:

1: A full investigation of all acts under Law 14.346, including seizure and analysis of all documented video evidence.
2: That his release not result in the case being shelved or stalled, and that charges reflect acts of cruelty (Art. 3), not a lesser offense.
3: That the case proceed to trial and the maximum penalty under the law be sought.
4: A ban on animal ownership and disqualification from contact with or care of animals.
5: Verification of the condition and welfare of the five rescued dogs at Refugio Soplo de Vida.
6: A public statement on the status of the case and full transparency — that developments and rulings be communicated publicly.

That someone presenting as a professional in animal behavior stands accused of these acts aggravates, not mitigates, the case.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/16yTkN8SAt_plMZAa1xLmyFvmoIlePVK7/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

A quien corresponda,

Por medio de la presente, denuncio y sigo el curso de un acto de crueldad animal para su investigación y sanción conforme al Artículo 261 del Código Penal del Estado de Coahuila de Zaragoza (delitos de crueldad y violencia contra los animales).

Liliana García ató a su perro Rocky, de 14 años, a su vehículo y lo arrastró por una vía pública en un barrio del norte de Saltillo. El acto fue captado en video, difundido en redes sociales y formalmente denunciado. El caso es competencia de la Fiscalía del Estado en Saltillo (Región Sureste).

Solicito a su oficina:

1: Integrar la carpeta de investigación y ejercitar acción penal en contra de Liliana García por el delito previsto en el Artículo 261, en el grado más grave que los hechos permitan.
2: Rechazar cualquier acuerdo reparatorio, criterio de oportunidad o mecanismo alternativo que permita que esta conducta quede impune.
3: Preservar el video, los dictámenes periciales y el expediente veterinario de Rocky como prueba.
4: Gestionar el decomiso de los animales bajo su cuidado y la prohibición permanente de tener o convivir con animales.
5: Emitir un comunicado público confirmando el ejercicio de la acción penal y dar a conocer públicamente los resultados de la investigación.

Rocky sufrió un acto de crueldad deliberada y prolongada a manos de quien debía protegerlo.

Evidencia en video: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1kP-Lvr_DQMNF4-u9EfW_KMFBlgkojvia/view?usp=sharing

Atentamente,

contact@hallieforanimals.org

The act was captured on video, reported on social media, and formally denounced. The matter falls within the jurisdiction of the State Prosecutor's Office in Saltillo (Southeast Region).

links.description:
𝐒𝐞𝐧𝐝 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐎𝐧𝐞-𝐂𝐥𝐢𝐜𝐤 𝐞𝐦𝐚𝐢𝐥 𝐢𝐧 𝐦𝐲 𝐛𝐢𝐨 𝐭𝐨 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐨𝐜𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐀𝐮𝐭𝐡𝐨𝐫𝐢𝐭𝐢𝐞𝐬 𝐭𝐢𝐭𝐥𝐞𝐝 "𝐏𝐫𝐨𝐭𝐞𝐜𝐭 𝐌𝐨𝐫𝐨𝐜𝐜𝐚𝐧 𝐒𝐭𝐫𝐞𝐞𝐭 𝐃𝐨𝐠𝐬"❗️

They're now shooting street dogs without shame in broad daylight.

Morocco is killing street dogs to "tidy up" the streets ahead of the FIFA World Cup 2030. People are filming “roundups” happening right outside homes and in front of kids.

It’s been proven time and time again that culling doesn’t solve stray populations or rabies. More dogs move in, breeding resumes except with fewer vaccinated dogs than before.

TNVR (trap, neuter, vaccinate, return) works . It cuts births, builds herd immunity, and steadily reduces numbers over time without the cruelty, and without the endless rinse-and-repeat of killing.

They're now shooting street dogs without shame in broad daylight.

Morocco is killing street dogs to "tidy up" the streets ahead of the FIFA World Cup 2030. People are filming “roundups” happening right outside homes and in front of kids.

links.mailtoBody:
To Whom It May Concern,

I am writing with urgent concern regarding the systematic and brutal killing of street dogs currently unfolding across Morocco, actions reportedly linked to preparations for the 2030 FIFA World Cup.

Shocking footage and eyewitness accounts reveal dogs being poisoned, shot, and discarded like trash. These killings are not only acts of cruelty—they are a humanitarian crisis in plain sight. If allowed to continue, they will stain Morocco’s reputation on the global stage and betray the very values of unity, dignity, and compassion that the World Cup is meant to embody.

This is a critical moment. Morocco can either stand as a model of humane progress or be remembered for silencing its stray population in cold blood before the games even begin.

We respectfully urge:

An immediate and total halt to the killing of street dogs.

The nationwide implementation of TNVR (Trap, Neuter, Vaccinate, Release) programs.

Collaboration with local and international animal welfare experts to develop ethical, sustainable solutions.

Morocco has the opportunity to lead by example—to show that greatness is measured not only in stadiums and goals, but in how a nation treats its most vulnerable. The world is watching. History is recording.

Please act now, before more innocent lives are lost, and the shadow of these killings becomes the defining image of Morocco’s World Cup legacy.

Sincerely,



السلام عليكم،

كنكتب ليكم بقلق كبير وبحالة استعجال على قتل الكلاب الضالة اللي واقع دابا في المغرب بطريقة وحشية ومنظمة، وكيقولوا أنها مرتبطة بتحضيرات كأس العالم 2030.

كاين فيديوهات وشهادات كتورينا الكلاب كتتسمم، كتضرب بالرصاص وكتترك تموت في الشوارع بحال شي حاجة ما عندها حتى قيمة. هاد التصرفات ماشي غير قسوة على الحيوانات، بل كارثة إنسانية كبيرة. إلى بقات هاد الحالة مستمرة، غادي تجرح سمعة المغرب قدام العالم وتناقض القيم ديال التضامن، الكرامة، والرحمة اللي خاص يكونو حاضرين فهاد الحدث العالمي.

هاد اللحظة مهمة بزاف. المغرب قدامو خيارين: يا إما يكون مثال للتقدم والإنسانية، يا إما يكون معروف بأنه قتّل كلبانو في دم بارد قبل ما تبدا المباريات.

كنطالبوا بكل احترام:

وقف فوري وشامل لقتل الكلاب الضالة.

تطبيق برامج التحصين، التعقيم، والإطلاق (TNVR) في جميع أنحاء البلاد.

التعاون مع جمعيات حماية الحيوان المحلية والدولية باش يلقاو حلول أخلاقية ومستدامة.

المغرب عندو الفرصة باش يورّي العالم باللي العظمة ماشي غير في الملاعب والنتائج، ولكن في كيفاش كيتعامل مع أضعف مخلوقاتو. العالم كيتفرج، والتاريخ غادي يسجل.

رجاءً تحركوا دابا، قبل ما تفقدو أرواح بريئة، وما توليش صورة هاد القتل هي اللي غادي تبقى فذاكرة كأس العالم فالمغرب.

مع فائق الاحترام

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

A dog at 146 Gibson Ln, Corpus Christi, TX 78406 (District 3) is kept tethered outside constantly with inadequate food, water, space and shelter. After rescuers began documenting the conditions, the owner moved the dog to the rear of the property to defeat inspection. The Golden Project Rescue has worked to resolve this for two weeks; offers to cover vet and grooming costs and to purchase the dog have all been refused, and the owner has become aggressive toward those attempting to help and is reported to have a prior criminal record. This is why the matter is directed to police as well as Animal Care Services.

Constant tethering without adequate shelter, shade, dry ground and potable water violates the Safe Outdoor Dogs Act (Texas Health & Safety Code Ch. 821, Subch. E). Failure to provide necessary food, water, care and shelter is a criminal offense under Texas Penal Code § 42.092, within CCPD's jurisdiction.

We demand that the City:

1: Conduct a welfare inspection at 146 Gibson Ln, 78406 without delay, with CCPD present to ensure officer and inspector safety given the owner's reported aggression and history, and to prevent a repeat where inspectors leave without seeing a dog that has been deliberately concealed.
2: If access is refused or the dog is hidden, obtain and execute a seizure warrant under Ch. 821, Subchapter B through the justice court and remove the dog.
3: Have CCPD assess the conditions under Penal Code § 42.092 and pursue charges if the threshold is met, independent of the civil tethering violation.
4: Publicly confirm that the inspection took place and release its outcome.

This has been documented and escalated for two weeks without enforcement. A dog is suffering now and the concealment is ongoing. Act on it.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1lg9OeRV_Cpj4qP8hu8YWu2Etj_JSDVrj/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

Two dogs; a doodle and a Yorkshire terrier are being kept on tethers at 500 W Ricky Crossland Ave (formerly 2nd St), Elsa, on the Austin Street side. One is tethered to a refrigerator. One is tethered to a vehicle parked on the public street.

The property; 500 W Ricky Crossland Ave, Elsa, 78543, Chandler's Addition, Lots 11 & 12, Block 2 is a rental. The record owners are not the occupants; the dogs are kept by the current tenant. Both dogs are tethered in view from the public street, so officers can observe the conditions without entry.

Texas Health and Safety Code § 821.102 prohibits leaving a dog outside and unattended on a restraint without adequate shelter, shade from direct sunlight, and potable water, and sets a minimum tether length of ten feet or five times the dog's body length. The restraint of each dog is a separate offence. The 24-hour warning period was repealed in 2022; officers may act immediately.

Under § 821.022, a peace officer who has reason to believe an animal is being cruelly treated may apply to a justice court for a warrant to seize the animal; on a showing of probable cause the court shall issue it and set a hearing within ten days. The conditions observable from the street supply that basis.

We demand:

1: A welfare check at this address today, with the vehicle tether treated as an immediate hazard.
2: Application for a seizure warrant under § 821.022 if conditions warrant.
3: Referral to the Hidalgo County District Attorney for assessment under Penal Code § 42.092.
4: Public release of the disposition of this report.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/13JQj-k64pdVWMXj_qZYHNBVFtTDqUhuh/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

On July 19, 2026, a Little Rock police officer shot and killed Ammo, a one-year-old Labrador, in the driveway at 4822 Country Club Blvd. Body-camera footage shows the officer ordering the owner to control the dog and backing several steps into the street before firing a single shot to the animal's head. Whatever the owner failed to do, the result was a killing that a taser, a tool LRPD's own policy authorizes against animals, could have prevented. The officer had the seconds it took to draw, aim, and fire. Those same seconds were available for a non-lethal response.

LRPD's policy made this outcome possible. It does not define when lethal force against an animal is justified. It explicitly treats the shooting of an animal as something other than a use-of-force incident, exempting it from the review every other firearm discharge receives. And the Little Rock Fraternal Order of Police has publicly stated the officer acted in accordance with department policy and training. We take them at their word, which is precisely why the policy and the training must change.

We call on the City of Little Rock to:

1: Revise General Order 303 to define when, if ever, lethal force against an animal is permitted, and to require de-escalation and non-lethal options — including the Taser already authorized — before any firearm is used.
2: Reclassify the discharge of a firearm at an animal as a use-of-force incident subject to the same review as any other use of force, ending the current exemption.
3: Mandate canine-encounter and animal-behavior training for all officers, using the U.S. Department of Justice COPS Office "Police and Dog Encounters" curriculum, available to departments at no cost.
4: Publicly release the findings of the review into Ammo's death and issue a public statement on the changes adopted.

Little Rock does not need a villain to fix this. It needs a procedure that stops treating a dog's life as beneath the standard applied to every other use of force. Ammo could not be blamed for what happened. He is the only one who paid for it.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1hllyjdwAJC7RZCm0HoHfZXbKFC_ygXNu/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

City of Stockton officers recovered one injured Siberian husky from Louis Park, near the Pixie Woods service entrance at 3121 Monte Diablo Ave. Your Animal Services records show when that recovery occurred. Three more huskies were abandoned at the same location and left behind. They remain on public park land, with no owner present and no one providing them food, water, or shade.

This is not a case with a missing address, an uncertain jurisdiction, or an access barrier. The location is City park land. Stockton Animal Services operates under the Police Department, and officers were physically on this site when the injured animal was taken. Under California Penal Code § 597.1, a peace officer with reasonable grounds to believe an animal is without proper care may take custody of that animal without a prior warrant. That authority applied to all four huskies at the moment officers arrived. Three were left anyway.

There is no lawful obstacle to collecting the remaining three, and there was none when officers first attended. What happened instead is that a documented, in-progress abandonment on public land was left half-addressed. Every day these animals remain, the City is choosing not to act on authority it already holds and has already exercised at this exact location.

We are not asking the Council to collect animals. We are asking the Council to account for why its own agency did not, and to direct that the job be finished.

We demand:

1: That Animal Services return to Louis Park and collect the three remaining huskies without further delay.
2: That their recovery be logged against the same incident as the injured husky already taken, so the full scope of this abandonment appears as one record.
3: That the City state publicly why three abandoned animals were left on public park land after officers were on scene and had already removed a fourth.
4: That the disposition of all four animals, the injured dog and the three left behind — be released publicly.
5: That the City confirm what steps it will take so that officers responding to multiple abandoned animals at one location do not leave any behind.

Officers have already been to Louis Park. They have already recovered one animal from it. Three are still there. Finish it.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1_pLT1I-P3_b1eYpVaFfLfmDxtFc5u6QZ/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.title: Protect Moroccan Street Dogs
links.mailtoSubject: Urgent Appeal – Halt the Mass Killing of Street Dogs in Morocco Ahead of FIFA 2030/ نداء عاجل – وقف القتل الجماعي للكلاب الضالة في المغرب قبل كأس العالم 2030
links.mailtoBody:
To Whom It May Concern,

I am writing with urgent concern regarding the systematic and brutal killing of street dogs currently unfolding across Morocco, actions reportedly linked to preparations for the 2030 FIFA World Cup.

Shocking footage and eyewitness accounts reveal dogs being poisoned, shot, and discarded like trash. These killings are not only acts of cruelty—they are a humanitarian crisis in plain sight. If allowed to continue, they will stain Morocco’s reputation on the global stage and betray the very values of unity, dignity, and compassion that the World Cup is meant to embody.

This is a critical moment. Morocco can either stand as a model of humane progress or be remembered for silencing its stray population in cold blood before the games even begin.

We respectfully urge:

An immediate and total halt to the killing of street dogs.

The nationwide implementation of TNVR (Trap, Neuter, Vaccinate, Release) programs.

Collaboration with local and international animal welfare experts to develop ethical, sustainable solutions.

Morocco has the opportunity to lead by example—to show that greatness is measured not only in stadiums and goals, but in how a nation treats its most vulnerable. The world is watching. History is recording.

Please act now, before more innocent lives are lost, and the shadow of these killings becomes the defining image of Morocco’s World Cup legacy.

Sincerely,



السلام عليكم،

كنكتب ليكم بقلق كبير وبحالة استعجال على قتل الكلاب الضالة اللي واقع دابا في المغرب بطريقة وحشية ومنظمة، وكيقولوا أنها مرتبطة بتحضيرات كأس العالم 2030.

كاين فيديوهات وشهادات كتورينا الكلاب كتتسمم، كتضرب بالرصاص وكتترك تموت في الشوارع بحال شي حاجة ما عندها حتى قيمة. هاد التصرفات ماشي غير قسوة على الحيوانات، بل كارثة إنسانية كبيرة. إلى بقات هاد الحالة مستمرة، غادي تجرح سمعة المغرب قدام العالم وتناقض القيم ديال التضامن، الكرامة، والرحمة اللي خاص يكونو حاضرين فهاد الحدث العالمي.

هاد اللحظة مهمة بزاف. المغرب قدامو خيارين: يا إما يكون مثال للتقدم والإنسانية، يا إما يكون معروف بأنه قتّل كلبانو في دم بارد قبل ما تبدا المباريات.

كنطالبوا بكل احترام:

وقف فوري وشامل لقتل الكلاب الضالة.

تطبيق برامج التحصين، التعقيم، والإطلاق (TNVR) في جميع أنحاء البلاد.

التعاون مع جمعيات حماية الحيوان المحلية والدولية باش يلقاو حلول أخلاقية ومستدامة.

المغرب عندو الفرصة باش يورّي العالم باللي العظمة ماشي غير في الملاعب والنتائج، ولكن في كيفاش كيتعامل مع أضعف مخلوقاتو. العالم كيتفرج، والتاريخ غادي يسجل.

رجاءً تحركوا دابا، قبل ما تفقدو أرواح بريئة، وما توليش صورة هاد القتل هي اللي غادي تبقى فذاكرة كأس العالم فالمغرب.

مع فائق الاحترام

To whom it may concern,

This is a request for a welfare check on a dog at the following location:

Building: Liv DTLA, 7th floor, 1411 Flower Street, Los Angeles, CA 90015

A dog has been observed over an extended period, kept out on the balcony of this unit for what appears to be nearly all of the time. The dog is repeatedly crying and barking at the door, consistent with distress and wanting to be let inside. There is concern that the animal may be enduring prolonged confinement, inadequate shelter, or a lack of proper care and attention.

An officer's attendance is requested to assess the dog's condition and living situation.

For reference regarding the department's authority to act: California Penal Code § 597.1 authorizes peace officers, humane society officers, and animal control officers to take custody of an animal that is neglected or otherwise cruelly treated. Where an officer has reasonable grounds to believe that prompt action is required to protect the health or safety of the animal, the statute directs the officer to seize the animal immediately and provide care, followed by a post-seizure hearing under § 597.1(f). The operative standard is reasonable grounds, not proof. Penal Code § 597f likewise authorizes officers to take possession of neglected or abandoned animals.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1W7rXiEcscTs7pub_0ElmTafXE6s0Pe5c/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing about the death of Prince, a 4-year-old French Bulldog, who died overnight while in the paid care of a pet sitter operating at 6622 Atlanta St, 33024. The apparent cause is heat exhaustion. No post-mortem examination has been conducted, and the family reports being told one is not possible. The sitter maintains multiple dog crates outdoors and continues to accept new bookings.

I am asking your office to:

1: Conduct an immediate welfare inspection of the property and of every animal currently in the sitter's care, including the outdoor crates and any confinement in heat.
2: Open an investigation into whether the conditions of Prince's death meet the threshold under Fla. Stat. §828.12 (cruelty) and §828.13 (confinement/failure to provide), and refer to the State Attorney if warranted.
3: Establish and confirm whether any post-mortem or veterinary examination remains possible, and preserve all veterinary, booking, and communication records relating to Prince.
4: Suspend the sitter's operation pending the outcome, so that no further animals are placed at risk while this is examined.
5: Issue a public statement and release the findings of the inspection and investigation publicly.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1asL-asotlny_nHBvDKz5knbl6ZYJ_U_y/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team

To whom it may concern,

On 26 July 2026, an elderly resident of A Wing, Royal Flora building, Palegaon, Ambernath East, was filmed on CCTV deliberately pushing a community cat from the 12th-floor duct wall to its death. The act was plainly intentional and is on camera.

I urge you to ensure this case proceeds to a full chargesheet and prosecution under Section 325 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, read with Section 11(1) of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960 — and that the CCTV evidence is seized and preserved, the accused identified, and the case not quietly closed. If it is claimed the accused is unwell, that is a matter for medical assessment and the court, not a reason to drop the matter.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1GDgl-17vxHGtUwC_NZYWqYdMcy0jU4zB/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

North Texas Pudelpointers, owned by Stephen Lundy of Paducah, Texas, is an active dog breeding and training operation. Footage circulating online appears to show Mr. Lundy restraining a dog on a raised table by a taut leash, arranged so that the dog must figure it out or choke, presented as a training method. The operation is ongoing.

We demand:

1: A welfare inspection of all dogs currently held at North Texas Pudelpointers.
2: An assessment by the appropriate authority of whether the conduct shown meets the threshold under Texas Penal Code §42.092 (cruelty to non-livestock animals), and referral to the County Attorney if warranted.
3: Review by NAVHDA and NAPPA of Mr. Lundy's documented conduct against their Code of Conduct and Code of Ethics, and of his continued standing.
4: A public statement of findings from each body, with full transparency once any review or inspection is complete.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1G87p5WbHuCkRib_ztGwPUINvGzBlNKiS/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

I'm writing to demand that the animal-cruelty case against Leandro Manuel R. D. detained after footage circulated of him beating two dogs with a bat in Posadas — proceed under national Law 14.346 to the full extent it allows, with no dismissal and no downgrade.

The conduct is documented on video. The complainant, his ex-partner, has reported prior abuse of the animals, and there is a parallel gender-violence case against him. Cruelty toward animals reliably precedes and accompanies violence toward people — this file already holds both.

To whom it may concern,

I am writing to file a formal complaint and demand full investigation and prosecution to the maximum extent of the law against the individual known as “Don Lenin” (or any other identification that appears in the case file) for dragging a dog tied to a vehicle in the López Arellano/Cerro Verde sector of Choloma, department of Cortés.

The video of the incident circulated widely and caused legitimate public outrage. A later public apology is not enough and does not extinguish criminal responsibility. Honduras’s Penal Code and the Law on Animal Protection and Welfare classify animal cruelty as a crime; when suffering or death is caused, penalties can include imprisonment and substantial fines.

I specifically request:

1: That the criminal complaint be formalized and pursued to the fullest extent.
2: That the current condition of the animal be investigated and that it receive immediate veterinary care if this has not already been done.
3: That the case not be shelved or reduced because of an apology or media pressure.
4: That the public be informed transparently about the progress of the case.

To whom it may concern,

Dhruv Das Tyagi, of Shalpura, recorded himself abusing a dog. The footage is in circulation and identifies him as the person responsible. This is a cognisable offence and requires immediate action.

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing to report an urgent animal-neglect emergency within Madera city limits. At least ten dogs are on the street behind the Pro Club & More store in the commercial center on Country Club Drive, just off the West Cleveland Avenue exit from Highway 99 (beside the Jack in the Box). The dogs have no water available to them and are exposed in dangerous heat. Without immediate intervention they will die.

The dogs are in a public place, so no property entry is required — your officers can respond to them directly. This is a deprivation of necessary drink and care under California Penal Code § 597, and § 597.1 gives your officers the authority to provide emergency care and take possession of animals found without adequate water or shelter. As unattended dogs at large in a public place, they are also subject to seizure and impound under the Madera Municipal Code.

I am asking the Department to:

1: Dispatch an Animal Control officer to the location immediately for an emergency welfare check, this is time-critical, not a routine complaint.
2: Provide the dogs with water and emergency care on arrival.
3: Take the animals into custody under Penal Code § 597.1 and the Municipal Code's impound authority.
4: Identify anyone responsible for placing or confining them there and pursue charges under Penal Code §§ 597 and 597.1.

Please treat this with the urgency it demands. Lives depend on how quickly your department responds.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1lpg_tsEDTkzNxqbGO1N1mKhnyN3RIe15/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing to demand action over the animal-cruelty incident at the Feria Regional del Rebozo, the event your municipality organizes. Video recorded at the fair on 6 August 2026 shows a person kicking a pony in the head while it was tethered to a carousel attraction, then fleeing. The animals were left unsupervised. As the organizer of this event, the Ayuntamiento is responsible for the welfare of every animal on the fairgrounds and for ensuring this assault is investigated.

I demand that the Ayuntamiento:

1: Identify the person responsible, using the fair's own live broadcast and recorded footage and the attraction operator's records, and file the corresponding complaint with the Fiscalía General del Estado so the case is investigated under Article 317 of the San Luis Potosí Penal Code.
2: Order an immediate veterinary examination of the pony that was struck, and a welfare inspection of every pony used in the attraction.
3: Suspend and remove the animal carousel for the remainder of the fair, consistent with the removal of animal attractions from FENAPO in 2025.
4: Issue a public statement on the measures taken, with full transparency on the outcome.

The footage is already public and widely shared. I expect a public account of what the Ayuntamiento has done in response.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1qQTWywz2q-8f3afQ0KIo75sIFNtpkRM-/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

A husky, "Sweetie," is emaciated, ribs and spine visible from across the lot, consistent with prolonged starvation. She has been reported repeatedly. No action has been taken.

Penal Code § 597.1 authorizes seizure of an animal, without a prior warrant, where prompt action is required to protect its health. Her condition meets that threshold now. The statute exists precisely so officers can intervene in situations like this one. Declining to use it is not neutrality, it is a decision to let the animal keep deteriorating.

Every day of inaction does concrete harm. Sweetie grows weaker. A visibly starving dog in a public place tells this community that Merced's cruelty laws will not be enforced. And a volatile situation left to fester does not stay contained, it endangers the public and the officers who will eventually have to respond to it, and that risk only grows the longer it is ignored. None of this is inevitable. All of it is within the power of the agencies receiving this email to prevent, today.

The residents of Merced fund Animal Services and the Police Department to act in exactly these circumstances. This is what their taxes pay for. Use the authority they fund.

Demands:

1: Seize Sweetie immediately under Penal Code § 597.1.
2: Perform a veterinary body-condition assessment on intake and preserve it as evidence.
3: Obtain and review CCTV from the adjacent Taco Bell for the relevant period; allegations of sexual abuse of the animal have been raised and must be investigated.
4: Publicly account for why repeated prior reports on this animal went unactioned.
5: Release the outcome of this intervention publicly.

Officers should be aware the owner is reported to be armed and possibly in mental health crisis; plan the approach accordingly, with crisis support if available. The public has been instructed not to approach.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1S8kxVqpCku_hMbU5X91wl0u0aqilT3lv/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

On the night of 7 August 2026, at around 11:08pm, a puppy lying in the road at 9/12 Springhill, Port Dickson, was run over by a Toyota Hilux, registration SAA 8272 B. The driver stopped, got out, looked at the dog he had struck, returned to the vehicle, reversed back over the animal, and drove away. This was not a road accident. Choosing to reverse over an animal you have already seen you hit is a deliberate act of cruelty that ended in that animal's death.

This conduct falls squarely within Section 29 of the Animal Welfare Act 2015 (Act 772) and amounts to mischief by killing an animal under Section 428 of the Penal Code. The vehicle is identified and traceable through JPJ records.

I call on you to:

1: Trace the registered owner and driver of Toyota Hilux SAA 8272 B without delay.
2: Open a formal cruelty investigation under Section 29 of the Animal Welfare Act 2015.
3: Refer the driver for prosecution under the Animal Welfare Act 2015 and Section 428 of the Penal Code once identified.
4: Coordinate with the Royal Malaysia Police so the deliberate nature of the act is pursued as a crime, not filed as a traffic matter.
5: Issue a public statement confirming the investigation, and release its findings publicly once concluded.

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing to urge your office to take the serious allegations of animal neglect and suffering at Downtown Ranch and Sanctuary/Dogtown Ranch (1279 FM 2116, Rockdale, TX 76567), owned by Angela Sera, with the full weight and ongoing attention they deserve.

A detailed Houston Press investigation (published July 27, 2026) documents extensive photographic and video evidence gathered by visitors and former volunteers between August 2025 and March 2026. These materials depict feces- and urine-covered floors and kennels, a decomposing dead pit bull left in front of other dogs, charred dog carcasses on burn piles, reports of dogs escaping and being killed in traffic, alleged fatal dog fights, and animals with untreated gaping wounds. Volunteers have expressed fear for the dogs’ welfare during extreme Texas heat, especially given the boarding fees the facility generates.

This stands in sharp contrast to earlier deputy responses that characterized complaints as “unfounded” after limited observations from the gate and notes of available food bags. While I acknowledge that your office has conducted subsequent unannounced inspections (including with outside animal-welfare professionals and a veterinarian), coordinated with groups such as SPCA of Texas, and reported that dogs had access to food and water and that the owner is making improvements and reducing numbers, the volume and graphic nature of the independent evidence raise legitimate public concern that conditions have been—and may still be—significantly worse than official walkthroughs have captured.

I respectfully request that your office:

1: Fully review and forensically evaluate all submitted photos, videos, and written complaints.
2: Conduct additional unannounced inspections with independent veterinarians and animal-cruelty specialists, focusing on the interior kennels, burn piles, medical records, and overall population management.
3: Ensure transparent follow-up so the public can have confidence that every animal’s welfare is being prioritized under Texas animal-cruelty statutes.
4: Continue close monitoring to verify that promised reductions in numbers and facility improvements are fully and sustainably implemented.

The dogs at this facility—many described as elderly, medically compromised, or difficult to place—depend on rigorous oversight. Public trust in local law enforcement’s handling of animal-welfare cases depends on thorough, evidence-based action.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/16s1FPkk6_VYACfKJFdhj8cdaERSgnZnh/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

Merced police department took Sweetie the husky into protective custody after a year of reports about her treatment by a homeless owner. Witnesses described her being dragged along hot pavement while her owner rode his bicycle. The president of the local SPCA said she personally saw him pick Sweetie up by the neck and slam her to the ground. Photos circulating online show her ribs clearly visible and a tight muzzle she appeared to be trying to remove. One video captures her yelping as she’s pulled by the collar off a folding chair.
Police say they spent weeks collecting evidence and submitted it to the Merced County District Attorney’s Office for review of potential animal cruelty charges. links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing as a concerned member of the community regarding the animal cruelty investigation involving the husky known as Sweetie and her homeless owner. Merced Police have taken Sweetie into protective custody and submitted the case to your office for review of potential animal cruelty charges under California Penal Code § 597 and related provisions.

Public reports, including coverage by ABC30 Action News, document numerous complaints dating back to last year, witness accounts of the dog being dragged on hot pavement while the owner rode a bicycle, the SPCA president stating she personally saw the dog picked up by the neck and slammed to the ground, circulating photos showing visible ribs and a tight muzzle, and video of the dog yelping while being pulled by the collar. Police have acknowledged receiving countless complaints and spending weeks collecting and submitting evidence. Lt. Kalvin Haygood has been quoted stating it takes time to build these cases and that the department is “hoping someone out there has the evidence we’re looking for.” With all due respect, it’s the police department’s job to investigate and canvas for CCTV footage, not to sit back and wait for someone else to do it for them.

Under Penal Code § 597.1, peace officers may seize animals when there are reasonable grounds to believe prompt action is required to protect the animal’s health or safety. Sweetie was examined by a veterinarian who reportedly found her in good enough health to return to the owner at one point, despite community observations of visible ribs; she was later taken into protective custody after additional reported incidents.

I urge your office to carefully review all submitted evidence, witness statements, photos, and video, and to file and pursue the strongest appropriate charges consistent with the facts and the law. Too often, animal cruelty cases are reduced or not pursued to the fullest extent; a strong response here would help ensure accountability, protect this animal from further harm, and send a clear message that neglect and abuse of animals will not be tolerated in Merced County. Please also seek appropriate orders regarding forfeiture of the animal and any restrictions on future animal ownership if a conviction results.

Thank you for your attention to this matter and for the work your office does on behalf of victims, including animals who cannot speak for themselves. I and many others in the community are watching this case closely and stand ready to support a thorough, justice-oriented resolution.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1RX4BS_TTjigOEBVmXtfr9coKwn4Whyur/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

Call:
Denton County DA: +1 940 349 2600

Location: Lewisville, Texas

Lynette Raesly, who ran Klink’s Canine Resort from her Lewisville home, is facing a felony animal cruelty charge after a family’s three-year-old Goldendoodle named Toby died while boarded with her.
The dog’s owner, Ilana Paikoff, had met Raesly, felt comfortable with the arrangement, and turned Toby over. Overnight, the dog’s AirTag began pinging away from the property. Investigators later determined Toby escaped through a large gap in an unsecured fence, was left unsupervised, and was found dead.
A neighbor told police Raesly had a history of dogs getting loose, some of which were never recovered. When officers executed a search warrant they found 13 dogs inside the home amid unsanitary conditions and no air conditioning. According to court documents, Raesly made only minimal efforts to locate or secure Toby and never left her property or called 911 or animal control.

To whom it may concern,

I am writing regarding the pending felony animal cruelty prosecution of Lynette Raesly of Lewisville, Texas, arising from the death of Toby, a three-year-old Goldendoodle, while under the care of her home-based boarding operation (Klink’s Canine Resort).

Pets are family members; negligence that results in preventable death, especially by someone holding herself out as a professional caregiver, demands strong accountability to deter similar conduct and protect animals in Denton County.

Thank you for your service and for prioritizing justice in this matter.

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing about the video circulating publicly that appears to show a uniformed LVMPD officer striking his K9 partner during a police response near Tropicana Avenue and Boulder Highway on August 11. The department has publicly acknowledged it is aware of the footage. I am calling on LVMPD to:

1: Open a formal Internal Affairs investigation into the conduct depicted, and confirm publicly that one is underway.
2: Immediately remove the officer from all K9 handling duties pending the outcome.
3: Order an independent veterinary examination of the dog and account for its welfare.
4: Hold the officer accountable under department policy and permanently bar him from working with police service animals.
5: Publicly disclose the findings and any disciplinary action taken.

A handler who strikes the animal placed in his care has no business working a K9 unit. The public is watching how LVMPD answers this.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1R5Yj_0EFgJ5Wtx9ZsNTtjiq_imJRya2O/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

A dog is being physically abused at 1377 Genessee Ave, Columbus, OH 43211. Video shows the person who keeps her striking her with a stick-like object. She is also kept tethered on the property. Columbus Humane attended this address and left her there. Children reside in the home.

Ohio Revised Code § 959.131(B) prohibits knowingly cruelly beating or committing an act of cruelty against a companion animal. § 959.131(C) makes knowingly causing serious physical harm to a companion animal a fifth-degree felony on the first offense under Goddard's Law. Beating a dog with a stick falls within these provisions. The tethering separately violates Columbus City Code § 2327.20 and the shelter and sustenance provisions of § 959.131.

Demands:

1: Seize the dog now under ORC § 959.132 and the authority you already hold, she is on video being beaten and cannot remain on that property.
2: Obtain and preserve the video and photographs as evidence.
3: Investigate and charge under ORC § 959.131 to the level the evidence supports, including the Goddard's Law felony provision (§ 959.131(C)) if the beating caused serious physical harm.
4: Enforce Columbus City Code § 2327.20 on the tethering.
5: Comply with Ohio's mandated cross-reporting duty under HB 33 (ORC 959.07–959.10): a child resides with the alleged abuser, notify Franklin County Children Services.
6: Publicly account for why the agency that already attended this address left a dog that video shows being beaten.
7: Release the outcome of this intervention publicly.

An agency has already been to this dog and left her where the abuse is happening, and there is video of her being struck. Every day of inaction is a day the law you are funded to enforce goes unenforced, and a child and an animal remain in a home you have already been called to. Use the authority the public pays for.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1tPnHer9HqCaalTU64kzqaUP1gIGsGA69/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

I'm reporting a dog found running at large in the City of Bell Gardens and requesting a welfare check and enforcement.

The visibly emaciated dog was found wandering the street alone and unsupervised. A member of the public gave her a hot dog and water, which she devoured. The owner, who arrived in a white Kia Telluride bearing California plate 9SJE066, states that a veterinarian has confirmed a diabetes diagnosis.

Whether or not that diagnosis is accurate, it does not explain or excuse the core problem: the dog was loose in public with no one in control of her. That is a violation of the leash/at-large ordinance and grounds for impound. If the dog is in fact diabetic, allowing a medically dependent animal to roam unsupervised and scavenge food is itself a serious failure of care, a managed diabetic dog is not left to wander the streets.

1: Conduct a welfare check on the dog and a licensed-veterinary body-condition assessment.
2: Impound the dog if she is found at large under the applicable leash/at-large ordinance.
3: If a diabetes diagnosis is claimed, require documentation of an active, veterinarian-supervised treatment plan — not merely an assertion of diagnosis.
4: Seize the dog under Penal Code 597.1 if she is being deprived of adequate food, care, or supervision.
5: Trace the registered owner via plate 9SJE066 if the dog and owner are not immediately located.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1iWRm7RMTg-oPixQlMmCDseDuKzWjSsmq/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

The RSPCA's Royal Patron is King Charles III. The "Royal" in your name was granted by Queen Victoria in 1840. The horses filmed in distress at Horse Guards are the King's own ceremonial guard.

You say you speak for every animal, in homes, in the wild, on farms, in laboratories. These horses are made to stand for hours as public photo props, in heat and crowds they have no say in, for a display with no purpose beyond spectacle, and it is done in the name of your own patron.

Publicly call for an end to the static public display of these horses.
State the RSPCA's position on the welfare of the King's ceremonial horses, on the record.

A charity that stays silent about animals suffering in the service of the Crown it serves should expect to be asked why.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xeR4Rij1gvKDbEHAnrm4Jrhecj6RF6IR/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,

To whom it may concern,

A man was filmed beating a cat with a stick in front of children in Auraiya district. An FIR has been registered and an arrest made. An arrest is only the first step — the case must now be carried through to conviction. I am asking you to:

1: Charge the accused under Section 325 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (mischief by killing, poisoning, maiming, or rendering useless an animal) read with Section 11 of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, and ensure the charge sheet is not diluted to the PCA Act alone.
2: Establish the cat's condition through veterinary or post-mortem examination so the charge reflects the severity of the injuries, and preserve that record.
3: Secure and preserve all evidence, including the video footage and the statements of the children and adults who witnessed the attack.
3: File the charge sheet within the statutory period and pursue the case to trial without delay.
4: Issue a public statement confirming the FIR number, the sections charged, and the status of the investigation.

This attack was witnessed by children and captured on video. How it is handled will show whether animal cruelty is treated as the cognizable crime the law now makes it. Please see it through.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1My276r76V5E0q8NLy6Plw4aqoseWrNDA/view?usp=sharing

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

Employees at Dames Bark Pet Grooming in O'Fallon filmed a husky that had become caught in a dangerous, inverted position on a grooming table. The dog was clearly distressed. Rather than free it, staff laughed, recorded it, and called the dog an idiot. The footage is circulating publicly.

A business that takes an animal into its paid care owes that animal a basic duty of care, and staff who film and mock a distressed animal instead of helping it have failed that duty. I am asking you to:

1: Open a cruelty investigation into this incident and into how Dames Bark Pet Grooming handles animals placed in its care.
2: Obtain and preserve the video footage and all relevant facility records, and identify the employees involved before evidence is deleted.
3: Determine whether the facts meet the thresholds of RSMo 578.009 (animal abuse) or 578.012 (animal neglect), and refer the matter to the St. Charles County Prosecuting Attorney for charging where warranted.
4: Inspect the facility's animal-handling and restraint practices — including grooming-table and restraint-loop safety — and its protocol for responding to an animal in distress.
5: Review the facility's operating status and any applicable licensing.
6: Issue a public statement and release the findings of the investigation publicly.

An animal cannot free itself from a restraint or speak for itself. The people paid to keep it safe are accountable for what happens while it is in their hands.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/114-L4i7-Ioy3-mm_pvP26SiYwV7AuF2Q/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

Florida has earned a national reputation for treating animal cruelty as the serious crime it is, from Ponce's Law to some of the strongest felony cruelty statutes in the country. That record is exactly why this case belongs in your hands, and why we're confident your office will meet it with the resolve Florida is known for.

On August 10, 2026, Martin County Sheriff's Office deputies removed 36 Border Collies from Paige O'Donnell's home at 1245 SW Alligator Street, Palm City. The dogs were matted, caked in feces and urine, and some were near-catatonic; groomers later found metal and glass embedded in their fur. The home was condemned as unfit for occupancy. O'Donnell now faces 72 charges — 36 felony counts of animal cruelty and 36 misdemeanor counts of improper confinement.

This was not a lapse. Martin County Animal Services responded to the property roughly 20 times since 2020. O'Donnell refused help from the Humane Society and the Sheriff's Office, built a fence system to wall the dogs off from view, and told investigators she had no more than five animals when there were 36. The Sheriff described her as a "calculated animal abuser." The record shows a sustained, knowing course of conduct.

We are asking your office to:

1: Prosecute all 72 counts to the full extent of Florida law, without reduction or consolidation of the felony charges.
2: Seek the maximum penalties available under Fla. Stat. §828.12 and §828.13, and pursue every aggravating factor the documented history supports.
3: Seek a permanent prohibition on O'Donnell owning, possessing, or having custody of any animal, as authorized under Ponce's Law.
4: Pursue permanent forfeiture of all 36 dogs so that none are ever returned to her custody.
5: Issue a public statement confirming the charges being pursued, and release the outcome publicly once the case concludes.

These dogs cannot testify to what four years in that house cost them. Their condition — and the years of documented warnings — speak for them. We're asking you to make that record count.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1593TW3w1_youuCswgXNQKFgJAzAh9tXw/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

I am writing to request an urgent investigation into footage circulating on Instagram depicting men deliberately killing a dog in what is believed to be the Tufanganj area of Cooch Behar district.

The footage, posted by the Instagram account @masum__ai___077____, shows at least two men using a stick to force a dog underwater in an apparent attempt to drown it. The men then coax the dog toward the bank, loop a rope around its neck to restrain it, and beat it repeatedly with a stick. The dog did not survive. The account holder appears to have filmed and documented the killing rather than participated directly, making him a key witness who can identify the perpetrators.

The account holder is believed to operate in the Tufanganj area of Cooch Behar district. This assessment is based on other footage posted by the same account, which shows a storefront on Tufanganj Main Road, specifically, the co-located Mio Amore and The Sugarr & Spice bakery outlets, that has been verified against Google Street View imagery. I respectfully urge your office to:

1. Serve a preservation and subscriber data request on Meta Platforms (Instagram) for the account @masum__ai___077____ before the content is deleted or the account is deactivated.

3. Identify and locate the men shown killing the dog in the footage.
4. Register a case under Section 11 of the Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960, and Section 325 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023, against the perpetrators once identified.

The footage constitutes prima facie evidence of the deliberate and prolonged killing of an animal. links.mailtoBody:
A quien corresponda:

Les escribo en relación con el caso de maltrato animal ocurrido en la comuna de La Florida, que se difundió ampliamente en las redes sociales entre el 24 y el 25 de agosto de 2026, y en el que se muestran actos de grave crueldad hacia uno o más animales.

El caso ya ha sido denunciado formalmente. El Colegio Licarayén confirmó que recibió la información, presentó una denuncia ante las autoridades y aplicó sus protocolos internos. La Municipalidad de La Florida condenó los hechos y ordenó a su equipo legal que presentara una denuncia ante el Ministerio Público. Les escribo, junto con muchas otras personas, para pedir que este caso no se estanque en la etapa de denuncia:

1: Investiguen los hechos de manera activa y oportuna, y no permitan que el caso se estanque.
2: Recopilar y preservar con urgencia las pruebas audiovisuales que circulan en las redes sociales antes de que sean eliminadas.
3: Verificar el bienestar y la seguridad de cualquier animal que aún se encuentre en el hogar o bajo el cuidado del responsable, coordinando con los organismos competentes según sea necesario.
4: Aplicar el artículo 291 bis del Código Penal y la Ley 21.020 («Ley Cholito»), dentro del marco procesal que corresponda.
5: Informar sobre el estado de la investigación en la medida en que lo permita la ley.

Entiendo que existen protecciones legales que rigen este tipo de casos, y no estoy pidiendo que se haga caso omiso de ninguna de ellas. Lo que pido es que la denuncia ya presentada sea investigada con seriedad y que la fiscalía actúe con la diligencia que exige la gravedad de estos actos.

Gracias por su atención y su compromiso con la justicia.

Prueba en video: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ZZvikKNewH0WFYWkEFgtGKtcXhmSP0gI/view?usp=sharing

Atentamente,



Equipo de @HallieForAnimals
contact@hallieforanimals.org





To whom it may concern,

I am writing regarding the animal cruelty case in the commune of La Florida, circulated widely on social media between August 24 and 25, 2026, showing acts of severe cruelty toward one or more animals.

The case has already been formally reported. Colegio Licarayén confirmed it received the information, filed a complaint with the authorities, and applied its internal protocols. The Municipalidad de La Florida condemned the acts and instructed its legal team to lodge a complaint with the Public Ministry. I write, alongside many others, to ask that this case not stall at the complaint stage:

1: Investigate the facts actively and promptly, and do not allow the case to stall.
2: Urgently collect and preserve the audiovisual evidence circulating on social media before it is deleted.
3: Verify the welfare and safety of any animal still in the home or under the responsible party's care, coordinating with the competent bodies as needed.
4: Apply Article 291 bis of the Penal Code and Law 21.020 ("Ley Cholito"), within whatever procedural framework applies.
5: Report on the status of the investigation to the extent the law permits.

I understand there are legal protections governing this type of case, and I am not asking that any of them be set aside. I am asking that the complaint already filed receive a serious investigation, and that the office act with the diligence the gravity of these acts demands.

Thank you for your attention and your commitment to justice.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ZZvikKNewH0WFYWkEFgtGKtcXhmSP0gI/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

On 11 August, West Yorkshire Police seized a seriously unwell Alsatian from a property on Market Street, in your constituency, after residents reported and filmed the dog being neglected, including that it had been left in a car during a heatwave. Its condition was so severe the dog had to be put to sleep. Aamad Ahmad has been charged with failing to prevent unnecessary suffering to an animal and is due before Kirklees Magistrates' Court on 2 September.

Your party promised better than this. Labour's 2024 manifesto pledged "stronger animal welfare" and called Labour the only party that can be trusted on it. Last December your Government launched a five-year Animal Welfare Strategy, billed as the biggest boost to animal welfare in a generation. Yet that Strategy is silent on the failure this case exposes: cruelty like this routinely ends in a suspended sentence, a token fine, and a disqualification order that no one enforces, leaving offenders free to walk into a rescue and collect another animal on the way home from court. The law allows up to five years, an unlimited fine, and a lifetime ban. Those powers are barely used, and your Strategy does nothing to change that.

You are the MP for the town where this happened, and you sit on the Government benches that wrote that Strategy. When a young life was lost to knife crime here, you issued a call to action and took it straight to ministers. I am asking you to do the same now:

1: Speak publicly to the strength of feeling this case has caused, and name the gap behind it, a Government that calls its own strategy world-leading while the cruelty already on the statute book goes under-punished.
2: Press for a mandatory, enforced national register of people disqualified from keeping animals, written into the Animal Welfare Strategy, so that a ban actually means something.
3: Support bringing animal cruelty within the Unduly Lenient Sentence scheme, so that sentences which fail the animal can be challenged in the Court of Appeal.
4: Ask ministers directly why the five-year maximum introduced in 2021 is so rarely used for offenses against pets, and what your Government will do to close the gap between the law and the sentences handed down.

Your party promised the biggest boost to animal welfare in a generation. Prove it here, on your own doorstep.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1YLrRjEJ0ZBNxXFbheljC7mZYGNiQTyuI/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

2. Localizar y asegurar al perro para garantizar su bienestar y brindarle atención veterinaria sin demora.

4. Examinar la responsabilidad del adulto que filmó el abuso sin intervenir.

La crueldad animal es un delito en el Estado de México. No debe quedar impune.

Two dogs are being kept in conditions of serious neglect at 2850 East South Street, Apartment 1, Long Beach, CA 90805. Long Beach Animal Care Services must:

1: Conduct an in-person welfare inspection of both dogs at 2850 East South Street, Apartment 1, without delay, and photograph their condition on arrival.
2: Seize both dogs under Penal Code § 597.1 if they are found without adequate food, clean water, or necessary care.
3: Ensure both dogs receive a licensed veterinary examination, including assessment and treatment of the matting and any underlying condition it is concealing.
4: Open a criminal investigation under Penal Code § 597(b).
5: Refer the matter to the Long Beach City Prosecutor for charging, and to the Los Angeles County District Attorney if the facts support a felony.
6: Issue a public statement confirming the outcome of the welfare check and make the findings publicly available.

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

Connecticut treats the deliberate torture of an animal as a felony, and was one of the first states in the country to give abused animals a voice in court through Desmond's Law. That standard is exactly why this case belongs in your office, and why supporters expect it to be met without compromise.

Marilyn Serenity Valdes of Waterbury has been charged with two counts of animal cruelty after she was recorded using a shock collar to make a caged dog yelp in pain, then repeatedly and aggressively jabbing the confined dog with a broom handle. The dog could not escape. This was not discipline or a moment of frustration, it was the deliberate infliction of pain on a trapped, defenseless animal, filmed as it happened.

Conduct like this falls squarely within Conn. Gen. Stat. § 53-247(b), the malicious and intentional torture and wounding of an animal, a class D felony. The recording removes any question of intent. Prosecute it as the crime it is:

1: Pursue both counts to conviction at the felony level the evidence supports under § 53-247(b), and resist any reduction to a lesser infraction or a simple neglect charge.
2: Oppose any application for Accelerated Rehabilitation or any other diversionary program that would erase this record. Recorded, intentional cruelty is not a candidate for diversion.
3: Move for the appointment of an animal advocate under Desmond's Law (Conn. Gen. Stat. § 54-86n).
4: Seek forfeiture of the dog and a prohibition on Valdes owning or living with animals.
4: Seek the full penalties available on conviction, including restitution for the animal's veterinary care.
5:: Make a public statement confirming the charges are being pursued, so this community knows torturing a caged animal carries consequences here.

The video is the evidence. Use it. Prosecute Marilyn Serenity Valdes to the full extent of Connecticut law.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1pCl8_0p_tvxMTHICWBjjFsSO7lKbvcGD/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

Just this July, your office took Gunner Cole Bush to sentencing for aggravated animal cruelty in Santa Rosa County. That result, alongside Ponce's Law and now Dexter's Law, is proof the First Circuit treats felony animal cruelty as the serious crime Florida law says it is. It's exactly why this case belongs in your hands, and why I'm confident your office will charge it to match the evidence.

David Kella Neely and Charolette Ann Dellinger, alleged French Bulldog breeders at 1535 Brigaten Ct, Gulf Breeze, FL 32566, were arrested after video showed them beating two of their French Bulldogs. The footage shows the dogs, which appeared to have escaped through a gap in the fence, struck repeatedly with an open palm and kicked, and one of the two can be heard screaming in pain, the sharp, unmistakable cry a brachycephalic dog makes under acute distress. After the beating, the dogs were pushed back through the same gap they had fled through. Both defendants were arrested, charged only with first-degree misdemeanor cruelty under Fla. Stat. §828.12(1), and released without bond. The dogs have reportedly since been removed from the property.

The misdemeanor charge does not match what the video documents. Section 828.12(2) makes it a third-degree felony to intentionally commit an act resulting in the repeated infliction of unnecessary pain or suffering, and that is precisely what the footage shows. These were not single reflexive strikes; they were repeated, deliberate blows directed at animals that posed no threat. The audible cry is direct evidence of pain. And forcing the dogs back through the fence gap shows control and intent, not panic. This was neither an accident nor a one-off.

Nor is it isolated. A second video has since surfaced showing Ms. Dellinger snatching a puppy by the scruff and wrenching it away from another person in a violent, aggressive manner. Two documented incidents, involving different animals, establish a course of conduct, the exact circumstance the statute's "repeated" standard is written for.

I'm asking your office to:

1: File aggravated animal cruelty charges under Fla. Stat. §828.12(2) against both David Neely and Charolette Dellinger, rather than proceeding on the first-degree misdemeanor.
2: Charge the abuse of each dog as a separate count.
3: Preserve the footage of both incidents.
4: Seek a permanent prohibition on both defendants owning, possessing, breeding, or selling any animal, as authorized under Ponce's Law.
5: Pursue permanent forfeiture of the dogs so that none are ever returned to their custody.
6: Confirm publicly which charges are being pursued once the filing decision is made.

The formal charging decision is still yours to make. These dogs were beaten by the people meant to care for them, and one of them screamed while it happened. The video leaves little to interpret. I'm asking you to charge this as the felony the evidence supports.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1sCpki_LkASuFKA0jbPbHCVko7OPDycqX/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

I'm also asking that each dog be charged as a separate count and that both be permanently barred from owning, breeding, or selling animals.

links.mailtoBody:
致相关人士：

贵校一名学生在Instagram上以“yuwenchaonan”的账号发布视频，将一只活的边境牧羊犬幼犬放入洗衣机，启动洗衣机，并拍摄了幼犬死亡的过程。幼犬最终死亡。该账号已被删除，但视频在删除前已广泛传播。

中国没有专门针对虐待动物的法律，但这完全属于贵校的管辖范围。根据教育部《高等学校学生管理条例》和贵校的学生纪律条例，学校可以对行为违反社会道德或严重损害学校声誉的学生进行处分，直至开除。故意虐待动物致死并拍摄视频的行为，既违反了社会道德，也严重损害了学校声誉。我要求清华大学：

1. 确认发布视频的“yuwenchaonan”学生身份（该账号已被删除），并核实其在校情况。

2. 根据贵校的学生行为和道德规范相关规定，对这起虐杀事件展开正式的纪律调查。

3：妥善保管已传播的视频以及所有已提交的关于此案的报告，作为证据。

4：如确认学生负有责任，应处以包括开除在内的最严厉处分。

5：将此事移交公安机关，追究其任何违法行为，包括扰乱公共秩序或拍摄、传播视频等。

6：发表公开声明，重申清华大学绝不容忍学生故意杀害动物的行为。

一旦知晓此事，清华大学的声誉将荡然无存。必须彻查此事，并采取相应行动。

视频证据：https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ynskuOsYPgfLS8z2BC1auHFZ7ViUNvyi/view?usp=sharing

此致，

@HallieForAnimals 团队

contact@hallieforanimals.org




To whom it may concern,

A student at your university, posting on Instagram as "yuwenchaonan," placed a live border collie puppy inside a washing machine, switched it on, and filmed the animal as it died. The puppy did not survive. The account has since been deleted, but the footage circulated widely before it came down.

China has no dedicated animal-cruelty statute, but this is squarely within your authority. Under the Ministry of Education's Regulations on the Management of Students in Regular Institutions of Higher Education, and your own student disciplinary regulations, a university may discipline, up to expulsion, a student whose conduct violates social morality or gravely damages the institution's reputation. Deliberately torturing an animal to death for a video does both. I am asking Tsinghua to:

1: Identify the student who posted as "yuwenchaonan," now that the account has been deleted, and confirm their enrollment.
2: Open a formal disciplinary investigation into the killing under your student conduct and social-morality provisions.
3: Secure and preserve the circulated footage and every report already submitted about this case as evidence.
4: Impose the maximum sanction available, up to and including expulsion, if the student is found responsible.
5: Refer the matter to public security authorities for any applicable offense, including any relating to public order or the recording and distribution of the footage.
6: Issue a public statement confirming that Tsinghua does not tolerate the deliberate killing of animals by its students.

This conduct is inseparable from the Tsinghua name the moment it is known. Investigate it, and act.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ynskuOsYPgfLS8z2BC1auHFZ7ViUNvyi/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

Your office's stated mission is the vigorous prosecution of crime and advocacy for the rights of every victim. Boomer had no voice of his own and no way to defend himself, and I'm writing because this case is exactly the kind your office exists to carry through, and because Florida law, strengthened by Ponce's Law and now Dexter's Law, treats felony animal cruelty as the serious crime it is.

In Sanford, Richardson Noel, an HVAC worker, kicked Boomer, a twelve-year-old dog weighing just five pounds, with such force that he knocked the dog unconscious and caused him to suffer a seizure. Noel has been arrested and charged with aggravated animal cruelty, bonded out, and fired from his job. The charge is already the right one. What matters now is that it is seen through.

This was not a moment of panic or a defensive reaction. Boomer is a small, elderly dog who posed no threat to anyone. Kicking an animal that size hard enough to render him unconscious and trigger a seizure is a deliberate act of violence against a defenseless victim — the excessive infliction of unnecessary pain and suffering that Fla. Stat. §828.12(2) was written to punish. That Noel was working in a position of access and trust when he did it only deepens the seriousness.

I'm asking your office to:

1: Pursue the aggravated animal cruelty charge under Fla. Stat. §828.12(2) to conviction, and reject any plea reduction, diversion, or dismissal that would drop it below a felony.
2: Preserve and authenticate all evidence — the arrest record, any video or witness statements, and the full veterinary record documenting that Boomer was knocked unconscious and suffered a seizure.
3: Seek a permanent prohibition on Richardson Noel owning, keeping, or living with any animal, as authorized under Ponce's Law.
4: Ensure that on conviction Noel is placed on the FDLE animal-cruelty offender registry, with no sealing or expungement, as Dexter's Law now requires.

Boomer was attacked by a stranger who had no cause and no excuse, and he survived a blow that could have killed a dog his size. The arrest was the first step. I'm asking you to finish it — to prosecute Richardson Noel to the full extent the evidence and the law allow.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/14x_QbhSavKNUxfxMB92-lUQwPmDA-sgj/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

To whom it may concern,

At least one dog is confined in a cage in the back of a truck at the intersection of Mariposa Avenue and James M. Wood Boulevard, Los Angeles. The vehicle's rear door is open, but the dog is caged and cannot leave, and there is no evident access to water. The vehicle carries California commercial plate 65473R1. A crated animal left unattended in these conditions requires a welfare check under California Penal Code § 597 and § 597.1.

An officer's immediate attendance is requested to:

1: Locate the truck (CA commercial plate 65473R1) at Mariposa Ave & James M. Wood Blvd and check the welfare of the caged dog(s), without delay.
2: Determine how long the animal has been confined and whether it has adequate water, and, given the vehicle is in the open on a sunny day, whether conditions potentially endanger it under Penal Code § 597.7.
3: Seize the dog(s) under Penal Code § 597.1 if found without necessary care, water, or shelter, or in distress, and arrange immediate veterinary assessment.
3: Identify the registered owner/operator and open an investigation under Penal Code § 597 as the findings support.
4: Treat this as time-critical: the vehicle is mobile and may leave at any point.

links.mailtoBody:
A quien corresponda:

Les escribo en relación con dos perros, un husky y un pitbull, que se encuentran en una vivienda ubicada en el Parque Residencial Paisajes, Etapa 1, Torre 2, Apartamento 1310, Bello, Antioquia. Desde hace aproximadamente cinco meses, una vecina ha denunciado en repetidas ocasiones que escucha golpes fuertes, objetos que se arrastran y que uno de los perros está siendo maltratado. Ha llamado a la policía más de ocho veces y se ha comunicado con la gestión ambiental y la administración del edificio, sin obtener una respuesta efectiva.

Solicito a las autoridades de Bello que tomen medidas:

1: Realicen sin demora una inspección presencial del bienestar de ambos perros y de sus condiciones de vida en esta dirección.
2: Apliquen las medidas correctivas previstas en la Ley 1801 de 2016 y procedan a la incautación preventiva, que la Ley 1774 de 2016 permite sin necesidad de una orden judicial previa.
3: Remitan el caso a la Fiscalía General de la Nación (GELMA) para que se inicie una investigación penal en virtud del artículo 339A del Código Penal, dado que las palizas repetidas pueden causar el daño grave que castiga dicho artículo.
4: Coordinar la respuesta entre la policía, la Inspección de Policía y la Fiscalía para que esto deje de ser un juego de pases entre oficinas, y asignarle a la denunciante un número de caso que le permita dar seguimiento.
5: Hacer público el resultado de la inspección y cualquier acción que se derive de ella.

Ningún animal debería vivir con miedo. Por favor, traten este asunto con la urgencia que merece.

Prueba en video: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1eueOz79Ve5jyRS8UR5ckh-Jbq3x5z__B/view?usp=sharing

Atentamente,



Equipo de @HallieForAnimals
contact@hallieforanimals.org





To whom it may concern,

I am writing about two dogs, a husky and a pitbull, kept in a residence at Parque Residencial Paisajes, Etapa 1, Torre 2, Apartamento 1310, Bello, Antioquia. For roughly five months a neighbor has repeatedly reported hearing heavy blows, objects being dragged, and one of the dogs being beaten. She has called the police more than eight times and contacted environmental management and the building administration, with no effective response.

I am asking the authorities of Bello to act:

1: Carry out an in-person welfare inspection of both dogs and their living conditions at this address without delay.
2: Apply the corrective measures available under Law 1801 of 2016, and exercise preventive seizure, which Law 1774 of 2016 permits without a prior court order.
3: Refer the case to the Fiscalía General de la Nación (GELMA) for criminal investigation under Article 339A of the Penal Code, given that repeated beating can cause the serious harm that statute punishes.
4: Coordinate the response across the police, the Inspección de Policía, and the Fiscalía so this stops being passed between offices, and issue the complainant a case number she can track.
5: Make the outcome of the inspection and any resulting action public.

No animal should live in fear. Please treat this as the urgent matter it is.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1eueOz79Ve5jyRS8UR5ckh-Jbq3x5z__B/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,
