links.mailtoBody:
A quien corresponda:

Les escribo en relación con el incidente ocurrido esta semana en Temperley, donde un estudiante, vistiendo el uniforme escolar, fue filmado pisoteando la cabeza de un gato en la vía pública. Este caso se encuentra actualmente bajo investigación por el fuero de menores. La crueldad animal deliberada por parte de un adolescente es una señal de alerta reconocida, asociada en estudios con violencia interpersonal posterior, y justifica una respuesta sustancial, más allá de una simple declaración pública. Solicito que se tomen las siguientes medidas:

1. Que el colegio aborde el incidente a través de su marco de convivencia y protección, con medidas concretas, en lugar de considerar la declaración pública como un asunto resuelto.

2. Que el estudiante reciba una evaluación psicológica y conductual profesional y el seguimiento adecuado, orientado a la evaluación e intervención, en lugar de la exposición o el castigo.

3. Que la investigación lleve a cabo un estudio exhaustivo, conforme a lo que exige la ley, sobre la personalidad del joven y sus circunstancias familiares y ambientales, en contacto directo con el adolescente y su familia.
4. Que se ordenen las medidas de protección y socioeducativas correspondientes con base en dicho estudio, para que el asunto no quede cerrado sin que se adopte ninguna medida.

5. Que dichas medidas incluyan evaluación y apoyo psicológico, dado el vínculo documentado entre el maltrato animal y la violencia interpersonal posterior.

6. Que se refuerce la educación en humanidad y empatía en todo el alumnado.

7. Que se confirmen públicamente las medidas concretas adoptadas.

No pido que se identifique al estudiante, y no lo identifico. Mi preocupación es la respuesta institucional y judicial, y que este adolescente reciba la intervención que requiere el momento.

Evidencia en video: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1jDZqXR0oVJrq8nqv0ee2YrHgUTTFmc42/view?usp=sharing

Atentamente,

Equipo @HallieForAnimals
contact@hallieforanimals.org




To whom it may concern,

I am writing regarding the incident this week in Temperley, in which a student wearing the school's uniform was filmed stomping on a cat's head on a public street — a case now under investigation by the juvenile fuero. Deliberate animal cruelty by an adolescent is a recognized warning sign, associated in research with later interpersonal violence, and it warrants a substantive response rather than a public statement alone. I ask that the following steps be taken:

1: That the school address the incident through its convivencia and safeguarding framework, with concrete measures, rather than treat the public statement as the matter resolved.
2: That the student receive a professional psychological and behavioral assessment and appropriate follow-up, directed at evaluation and intervention rather than exposure or punishment.
3: That the investigation carry through in full the study the law requires into the young person's personality and his family and environmental circumstances, in direct contact with the adolescent and his family.
4: That the corresponding protective and socio-educational measures be ordered on the basis of that study, so the matter is not closed without any measure adopted.
5: That those measures include psychological assessment and support, given the documented link between animal cruelty and later interpersonal violence.
6: That humane and empathy education be strengthened across the student body.
7: That the concrete measures adopted be confirmed publicly.

I do not ask that the student be identified, and I do not identify him. My concern is the institutional and judicial response, and that this adolescent receives the intervention the moment calls for.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1jDZqXR0oVJrq8nqv0ee2YrHgUTTFmc42/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org

links.mailtoBody:
To whom it may concern,

You built Westchester's first dedicated animal cruelty unit. You have publicly called what was done to Milo cruel and callous, and said there is never an excuse for it. This case is where that record is tested, and supporters expect it to be met with the charge the evidence supports, not a lesser one.

Milo, a 14-pound terrier, was entrusted to the Dogtopia facility in Peekskill for daycare. He came home unable to walk properly, off his food, and lethargic. A veterinary exam found bruising across his abdomen consistent with blunt-force trauma. That discovery led to the facility's own internal CCTV, which captured employee Cole Kamrath abusing him. Dogtopia fired him and called police, and he was arrested and charged. This was not rough handling. It was the deliberate beating of a small, defenseless dog who could not get away, inflicted by the very person paid to care for him, and caught on camera.

Conduct like this belongs under Agriculture and Markets Law § 353-a, aggravated cruelty to animals, Buster's Law, a felony. Milo is a companion animal under § 350. The internal footage establishes the aggravated, deliberate manner. 

The veterinary findings, abdominal bruising, blunt-force trauma, loss of mobility, go to intentional serious physical injury. Charge it as the crime it is:

1: Prosecute this as aggravated cruelty under § 353-a, the felony, not the § 353 misdemeanor that cases like this too often default to.
2: Refuse any plea reduction to a misdemeanor, and oppose any diversion or conditional discharge that would clear this from his record. Recorded, deliberate injury to a dog in paid care is not a candidate for a slap on the wrist.
3: Secure and preserve the original CCTV and the certified veterinary records, including imaging and the prognosis on Milo's mobility, as the backbone of the serious-injury element.
4: Seek a court order barring Cole Kamrath from owning, working with, or having custody of animals. He abused a dog inside a professional pet-care facility; he should not be trusted with another.
5: Seek the full penalties available on conviction, including restitution for Milo's veterinary care.
6: State publicly which charge level your office is pursuing, so this community knows that abusing an animal entrusted to professional care carries real consequences here.

The footage exists. The injuries are documented. His own employer watched it, fired him, and called the police. Charge it as the felony it is. Prosecute Cole Kamrath under § 353-a.

Video evidence: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1VW1YnYKDaepe1MzVX54gdhCt0rgOualy/view?usp=sharing

Sincerely,



@HallieForAnimals Team
contact@hallieforanimals.org
